# Husband-Wife Led Skippi Sees Revenue Fall 60% to Rs 8.2 Cr in FY25; Amid Lower Losses

Skippi’s revenue fell 60% to Rs 8.2 Cr in FY25, while losses narrowed to Rs 6.3 Cr, reflecting improved cost control despite weaker sales performance.

![ ](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/100x0/filters:format(webp)/startuppedia/media/member_avatars/2026/05/11/2026-05-11t151814780z-whatsapp-image-2026-05-11-at-204741-2026-05-11-20-48-15.jpeg )

Ravi Kabra and Anuja Kabra—Founder of Skippi

Icepops brand Skippi recorded a 60% decline in revenue to Rs 8.2 crore in FY25, down from Rs 20.2 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). 

Revenue from domestic sales of ice pops stood at Rs 7.2 crore in FY25, nearly half of Rs 14.5 crore in FY24, while exports contributed Rs 1 crore during the year.

On the expense front, total expenses declined by 56% to Rs 14.8 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 33.4 crore in FY24. Employee benefit expenses fell to Rs 5.3 crore from Rs 11.5 crore in the previous year. 

Advertisement and promotion expenses remained largely stable at Rs 2.5 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 2.3 crore in FY24. 

![TBI Logo](https://static-cdn.publive.online/english-betterindia/media/media_files/2025/10/06/gda-logo-light-2-2025-10-06-15-39-59.png)

The company’s losses narrowed to Rs 6.3 crore in FY25 from Rs 13 crore in FY24. On average, the company spent Rs 1.80 to earn every rupee in FY25.

## About Skippi

Skippi Ice Pops is an Indian frozen treats brand based in Hyderabad, founded in 2021 by husband-and-wife duo Ravi Kabra and Anuja Kabra. 

The brand specializes in 100% natural, preservative-free ice pops and gained national recognition after appearing on Shark Tank India Season 1, where it became the first company to secure an “All-Shark” deal from all five investors. 

Skippi focuses on nostalgia-driven “chuskis” (ice sticks) with a modern, health-conscious twist. Its products are available across multiple channels, including its official website for direct and B2B orders, e-commerce platforms such as Amazon India, Flipkart, and BigBasket, and quick commerce platforms like Zepto, Blinkit, and Swiggy Instamart for rapid delivery in major cities. 

Offline, the brand has a presence in over 10,000 retail outlets across India. In August 2022, the company introduced “Skippi Freezer Bikes” under a new franchise vertical, offering a modern take on traditional ice pop selling through electric bikes equipped with freezers, while also creating opportunities for aspiring entrepreneurs.

Kapiva's total expenditure rose 31.2 percent to Rs 547 crore in FY26 from Rs 417 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses remained its highest cost, increasing 39.8 percent to Rs 260 crore from Rs 186 crore and accounting for nearly 48 percent of total expenditure.

Procurement costs grew 22.6 percent to Rs 117 crore, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 78 crore. Despite higher spending, losses remained relatively stable at Rs 72 crore, compared with Rs 69 crore in FY25. [...] Total expenditure rose 38 percent to Rs 1,576 crore from Rs 1,140 crore. Legal and professional expenses increased 6.8 percent to Rs 550 crore from Rs 515 crore, including payments to astrologers. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses declined 56 percent to Rs 63 crore, largely due to lower ESOP-related costs. [...] The increase in spending impacted profitability, resulting in a sharp rise in losses. Oziva reported a net loss of Rs 18.5 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 4.2 crore in FY25. The company noted that cash-settled ESOP expenses contributed significantly to the loss as employees exercised stock options following changes in ownership. Excluding the Rs 22 crore ESOP-related cost, Oziva would have reported an estimated profit of around Rs 3.5 crore.

At the end of FY26, the company’s cash and bank balance stood at Rs 8.8 crore, down 67 percent year-on-year, while current assets totaled Rs 106 crore.

Skippi Ice Pops - India’s 01st Ice Popsicle brand - received funding of a whopping Rs 10 million for 15 percent equity in the 1st edition of Shark Tank India aired on Sony Entertainment Television.

Led by Kabra Global Products Pvt. Ltd., India, Skippi Ice Pops was launched with an aim to introduce a fun new product in the F&B category by husband and wife duo, Ravi Kabra and Anuja Kabra.

Skippi Ice Pops created history becoming the 1st brand on Shark Tank India to receive an 'All Shark Deal'.

Impressed by the pitch and the product, Skippi Icepops received backing from all 5 sharks - Ashneer Grover, MD, and Co-Founder, Bharat Pe, Anupam Mittal, Founder and CEO, Shaddi.com, Aman Gupta, Co-Founder and CMO, boat, Vineeta Singh, CEO and Co-Founder, SUGAR Cosmetics, NamitaThapar, Executive Director and Emcure Pharmaceuticals.

Skippi Ice Pops is here to bring back a part of our childhood while allowing parents to introduce one of the most loved treats to their children with a product that is 100 percent natural and created with stringent hygiene standards.

Ravi Kabra, Co-Founder of Skippi Ice pops said, “We are delighted to receive funding from Shark Tank India, it is a testament to our idea of creating disruption in the F&B industry with innovation and research. We plan to invest this amount to drive more innovation and introduce more refreshing flavors to the Indian market.”

Currently available for purchase in six exciting flavors; Raspberry, Orange, Cola, Mango Twist, Bubblegum, and Lemon, across all major online marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart, Qtrove, and at several states with distributor chain.

The brand is currently available in over 660 outlets in Hyderabad alone, 2,200 outlets across India, and continue to grow. It is priced at Rs 240 for a paper box of 12 pops with 6 flavors and Rs 666 for a bag of 36 pops.

Astrotalk FY26 Results Show Strong Profit Growth and International Expansion

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Astrotalk FY26 Results Show Strong Profit Growth and International Expansion](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/GIVA%20turns%20Diwali%20firecrackers%20into%20jewellery%20in%20new%20campaign%20%2810%29.jpg)

Astrology and spiritual wellness platform Astrotalk reported a more than tenfold increase in net profit to Rs 222 crore in FY26, while revenue from operations grew 55 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,823 crore from Rs 1,176 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements. **The growth was supported by international expansion and rising sales from its e-commerce business.**

**The Noida-based company connects users with astrologers through paid consultations via chat, voice calls, and video.** Revenue from consultations increased 45 percent to Rs 1,657 crore from Rs 1,139 crore, accounting for around 91 percent of operating revenue in FY26.

**International markets emerged as a key growth driver, with overseas revenue rising 2.6 times to Rs 621 crore from Rs 236 crore.** International operations contributed 34 percent of total revenue, compared with 20 percent a year earlier. **Revenue from India grew 28 percent to Rs 1,202 crore, while overseas markets added Rs 385 crore in revenue during the year.**

**Astrotalk also expanded its e-commerce operations through Astrotalk Store, which sells Rudraksha, gemstones, crystals and Vastu products through its website and marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit.** Revenue from this segment increased 4.4 times to Rs 166 crore in FY26 from Rs 37 crore in FY25.

> **Puneet Gupta, Founder and CEO, Astrotalk said**, “We set out to build a diversified, global business from India, and FY26 shows it is working. A third of our revenue now comes from outside India, and Astrotalk Store has grown into a real second business.”

**Total expenditure rose 38 percent to Rs 1,576 crore from Rs 1,140 crore.** Advertising and business promotion expenses more than doubled to Rs 823 crore from Rs 337 crore, accounting for 52.2 percent of total expenses. Legal and professional expenses increased 6.8 percent to Rs 550 crore from Rs 515 crore, including payments to astrologers. **Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses declined 56 percent to Rs 63 crore, largely due to lower ESOP-related costs.**

**Astrotalk's return on capital employed stood at 30.8 percent, while its EBITDA margin reached 13.83 percent.** The company spent Re 0.86 for every rupee earned in operating revenue during FY26. As of March 2026, its current assets stood at Rs 653 crore, including Rs 141 crore in cash and bank balances. **The company's ability to sustain international growth while managing marketing costs and diversifying revenue beyond consultations will remain important to its future financial performance.**

Ather Energy Turns Profitable in Q2 FY27 as Revenue Reaches Rs 1,464 Cr

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Ather Energy Turns Profitable in Q2 FY27 as Revenue Reaches Rs 1,464 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-26T145851.966.jpg)

Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1.3 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 154.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. **The company had posted a net loss of Rs 51.1 crore in the June quarter of FY27.**

**Ather Energy's operating revenue increased 62.9 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,464.2 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 898.9 crore in the year-ago period.** On a sequential basis, revenue grew 20.3 percent from Rs 1,216.9 crore in Q1 FY27.

Including other income of Rs 62.7 crore, **the company's total income reached Rs 1,527 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 940.7 crore in the corresponding period last year.**

**Despite reporting its first quarterly net profit in the period under review, Ather's operating revenue remained below its total expenses.** The company's operating revenue was Rs 61.5 crore lower than its overall expenditure, highlighting the contribution of other income to its reported profitability.

**The development follows an improvement in the company's operating performance in the June quarter, when Ather Energy reported positive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of Rs 9 crore.** However, it continued to report a net loss of Rs 51.1 crore in Q1 FY27.

**Ather's total expenses rose 39.4 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,526 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,094.7 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.** The increase was slower than the growth in operating revenue during the period.

Alongside its financial results, **the electric vehicle manufacturer announced plans to expand its annual manufacturing capacity by a combined 2.25 lakh units across its existing Hosur facility and the upcoming Factory 3.0 in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra.**

**The planned capacity expansion is expected to support Ather Energy's manufacturing requirements as it continues to grow its electric two-wheeler business.**

The latest results reflect an improvement in revenue growth and reported profitability, while the planned manufacturing expansion signals the company's focus on increasing production capacity to support its next phase of growth.

![Kapiva Revenue Nears Rs 465 Cr in FY26 as Offline Sales Grow 81 Pc](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20Design%20-%202026-10-27T131543.672.jpg)

Ayurvedic wellness brand Kapiva reported a 36.5 percent year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 464 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 340 crore in FY25. **Following 50 percent revenue growth in the previous fiscal year, the company continued expanding while keeping its losses broadly stable.**

**Including Rs 10 crore in non-operating income, Kapiva's total income reached Rs 474 crore in FY26.** Founded in 2015, the company sells Ayurvedic nutrition and wellness products across categories such as diabetes management, liver health, women's hormonal health, energy, and sports nutrition.

**Kapiva's total expenditure rose 31.2 percent to Rs 547 crore in FY26 from Rs 417 crore in FY25.** Advertising and promotional expenses remained its highest cost, increasing 39.8 percent to Rs 260 crore from Rs 186 crore and accounting for nearly 48 percent of total expenditure.

**Procurement costs grew 22.6 percent to Rs 117 crore, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 78 crore.** Despite higher spending, losses remained relatively stable at Rs 72 crore, compared with Rs 69 crore in FY25.

**Excluding employee stock option (ESOP) expenses of Rs 7.85 crore, the company's EBITDA margin improved to -14.8 percent from -18.7 percent a year earlier.** Kapiva spent Rs 1.18 for every rupee of operating revenue generated.

**The company has invested in expanding its product portfolio and offline distribution infrastructure, particularly in liver care, cholesterol management and women's hormonal health.**

> “During the last year, Kapiva has made significant investments in creating new categories (Liver Care, Cholesterol, Women’s Hormonal Health) and building infrastructure for offline distribution. These investments are likely to deliver substantial leverage in coming years which helps drive profitability,” **a company spokesperson said.**

**In FY26, Kapiva's lifestyle diseases category grew 114 percent year-on-year, while daily wellness increased 66 percent and women's health rose 21 percent.** Sports nutrition and energy recorded 5 percent growth.

**Offline sales led channel expansion, growing 81 percent year-on-year. Marketplace revenue increased 34 percent, while the direct-to-consumer (D2C) channel grew 21 percent.** The average order value on its D2C platform stood at approximately Rs 1,200, with repeat purchases contributing nearly 55 percent of D2C revenue.

**Kapiva reported an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of approximately Rs 650 crore to Rs 700 crore and aims to achieve a low-single-digit positive EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27.**

**The company has raised around $90 million to date, including a $60 million Series D funding round led by 360 ONE Asset and Vertex Growth.** Its revenue has grown approximately 93 percent over two years, from Rs 240 crore in FY24 to Rs 464 crore in FY26.

![Nutrifresh Plans Southern India Expansion With Rs 400 Cr FY27 Revenue Target](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-23T151200.430.jpg)

Indian controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) company Nutrifresh reported revenue of Rs 219.3 crore in FY26, registering a 51 percent increase from Rs 145.2 crore in FY25. **The company is targeting Rs 400 crore in revenue for FY27, driven by farm capacity expansion, institutional funding and rising demand from quick-commerce platforms, modern retailers and hospitality businesses.**

Founded in 2019, Nutrifresh has remained profitable since its inception. The company currently operates 83 acres of farmland and has an additional 105 acres under construction at Warwadi and Pisavare near Pune. **The new facilities are expected to increase its production capacity as it prepares for the next phase of growth.**

**During FY26, Nutrifresh and Rural Enhancers Group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Maharashtra government to develop a 1,000-acre smart-agriculture project.** The company also secured an initial tranche of Rs 90 crore from the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), forming part of a proposed Rs 400 crore investment to expand its controlled-environment agriculture infrastructure.

**Nutrifresh supplies produce to more than 100 large business customers across the hotel, restaurant, modern retail and quick-commerce segments.** Its client base includes Swiggy, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, BigBasket, Reliance Fresh, Nature’s Basket, IHCL and Taj SATS. The company distributes its produce across 15 Indian states and international markets, including the UAE, Maldives and Singapore.

**The company employs more than 650 people, with women accounting for 60 percent of its workforce.** Women represent 80 percent of its farm-level employees and more than 43 percent of leadership positions.

**For FY27, Nutrifresh expects its productive farmland footprint to nearly triple and is preparing to expand its operations across southern India.** It is also scaling its Joint Farming model, which enables farmers to grow produce on their own land in partnership with the company. **The approach is intended to increase production without requiring equivalent capital investment in company-owned farms.** Nutrifresh has set a long-term ambition to support more than 25,000 farmers through this model.

**Co-founder, CEO and Whole-Time Director Sanket Mehta attributed the company's growth to its proximity to urban markets, business-to-business distribution network and investments in crop-specific technologies.** CFO and Whole-Time Director Ganesh Nikam highlighted disciplined capital allocation, investor support and strategic partnerships as important factors supporting the company's expansion.

With increasing revenue, additional farmland, and institutional funding, Nutrifresh is focusing on scaling its technology-led agricultural operations while maintaining profitability and expanding its supply network across India.

Harajuku Tokyo Café, the Japanese food and beverage company operating Harajuku Tokyo Café and Harajuku Bakehouse, has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Zero W. **The company plans to use the capital to expand its outlet network, strengthen its operational infrastructure, and enter additional Indian markets.**

**Existing investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC participated in the round through follow-on investments.** New investors include Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Rahul Jain, co-founder of Epigamia, and others.

**The latest funding follows a $2 million (Rs 19 crore) seed round raised in August 2025.** The round was co-led by IAN and Samved VC, with participation from LetsVenture and venture debt fund Capitar Ventures.

Harajuku Tokyo Café is targeting revenue of Rs 100 crore in the current financial year. **The fresh capital will support its next phase of growth as it expands across existing and new markets.**

**Founded in 2021 by Gaurav Kanwar, the company operates two food and beverage formats across Delhi NCR and Mumbai.** Harajuku Tokyo Café is a full-service dining concept featuring conveyor-belt sushi and Tokyo-inspired interiors, while Harajuku Bakehouse operates as a quick-service format offering Japanese breads, desserts and savoury snacks.

**The company has developed its menu and operating model in collaboration with chefs Asami Indo and Higuchi Nariaki, with a focus on introducing contemporary Japanese food to Indian consumers while building a platform for expansion.**

**Over the next two quarters, Harajuku plans to open 10 outlets across new neighbourhoods in Delhi NCR and Mumbai.** It is also preparing to enter Bengaluru and Chandigarh. In addition, the company aims to make its central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru operational by December 2026. These facilities will supply Harajuku Bakehouse outlets and support packaged food production for markets in western and southern India.

**Since its seed funding round in August 2025, the company has doubled its outlet count and revenue.** Mumbai, where the brand began operations in July 2025, now contributes 25 percent of its revenue. The business processes more than 1,000 orders daily across dine-in and delivery channels.

**Harajuku Bakehouse accounts for over 30 percent of the company’s total revenue.** In Delhi NCR, the brand sells more than 1,000 loaves of bread each week through quick commerce platform Blinkit. Harajuku plans to extend the Bakehouse format to additional metropolitan markets as it expands its presence in India’s food and beverage sector.

Nandani Creation Limited, the company behind women's Indian wear brand Jaipur Kurti, has opened four retail stores in a single day under Project 50, its expansion initiative aimed at increasing its store network from 18 to 50 by March 31, 2027.

**The newly opened outlets are located at DT Mega Mall in Gurgaon, Jammu, Pacific Mall in Jaipur, and Rajouri Garden in Delhi.** The openings mark a step forward in the company's efforts to expand its retail footprint and strengthen its presence across key markets.

**Announced in September 2026, Project 50 focuses on expanding Jaipur Kurti's exclusive brand outlets while integrating its physical stores with its direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform and online marketplaces.** The company is also investing in product development, technology adoption, artificial intelligence-led business insights, analytics, and inventory management to improve operational efficiency and support its growth plans.

**Jaipur Kurti operates through company-owned, company-operated (COCO) and franchise-owned, franchise-operated (FOFO) stores.** Its retail presence also extends to departmental stores and shop-in-shop formats. The brand's retail partners include Shoppers Stop, Reliance Trends, Avantara, Kalanikethan, Reliance Centro, Fashion Factory and Lulu Malls.

**In the online segment, Jaipur Kurti sells through platforms such as Myntra, AJIO, Nykaa, Flipkart and Tata CLiQ, alongside its official website and mobile application.** The company has also entered the quick-commerce segment through Swiggy Instamart, expanding its distribution channels.

> **Anuj Mundhra, Chairman and Managing Director, Nandani Creation Limited said**, “Project 50 is moving from vision to execution. Opening four stores in a single day is an encouraging milestone and reflects our determination to translate our growth ambitions into measurable progress. Our objective is not simply to expand our retail footprint, but to build a scalable and integrated business that delivers stronger customer reach, better operating efficiency, and sustainable growth. As we move towards our target of 50 stores by March 2027, disciplined execution and long-term value creation will remain at the heart of our strategy.”

**Founded in 2012, Nandani Creation Limited is a Jaipur-based, online-first fashion company specialising in women's Indian wear.** Its portfolio includes Jaipur Kurti, Amaiva – By Jaipur Kurti, Jaipur Kurti Luxe and Desi Fusion. Headquartered in Jaipur, the company operates through a combination of digital commerce platforms and physical retail outlets as it continues to expand its market presence.

Health and wellness platform aiqa has entered the direct-to-consumer (D2C) healthcare market, marking a shift from its employer- and partner-led business model to direct consumer engagement. **After operating exclusively through employers and business partners for six years, the company is now expanding its services to individuals through a dedicated online platform.**

**Through its new website, aiqa will provide consumers with health plans and preventive healthcare programmes.** Its first D2C offering is a doctor-led weight management programme, with additional healthcare and wellness services expected to be introduced in the coming months.

**Backed by Eleven, aiqa currently generates approximately Rs 100 crore in revenue and adds nearly 1 lakh members every month across more than 500 cities.** The move into D2C is expected to help the company establish direct relationships with consumers while broadening access to its healthcare services beyond employer-sponsored and partner-led channels.

**To support its new business direction, the company has introduced an updated brand identity and a redesigned website.** The new platform will serve as the primary digital channel for its consumer-facing healthcare services, allowing individuals to access its offerings without relying on employer or business partnerships.

**Alongside its D2C expansion, aiqa has appointed Anuj Arora as Chief Executive Officer to lead its partner- and employer-focused business.** Arora brings 23 years of professional experience across India, Southeast Asia and Hong Kong. He previously served as Executive Vice President and Business Head at MediBuddy. **His experience also includes leading Monster's India small and medium-sized business (SMB) division and its operations in the Philippines and Hong Kong.**

**The company's consumer strategy builds on the healthcare infrastructure, operational capabilities, and member base developed through its existing business.** While aiqa will continue serving employers and partners, its D2C model is intended to reach individuals seeking more proactive and personalised healthcare solutions.

Weight management and preventive healthcare will form the initial focus of the consumer platform, with plans to expand into other wellness and personalised healthcare services over time.

SORRY SUGAR, a zero-added-sugar beverage and consumer brand, has announced the appointment of Palash Arneja as its Founder and Chief Executive Officer, as the company looks to accelerate growth and expand its presence in India’s fast-growing better-for-you products market.

**The leadership announcement comes at a time when consumers are increasingly seeking healthier alternatives without compromising on taste, creating new opportunities for brands focused on wellness-driven innovation.**

Arneja, who previously built BLA BLI BLU into a Rs 1,000 crore brand within a year, has been associated with SORRY SUGAR since its incubation alongside Wolfpack Labs. **In his new role, he will oversee the company’s long-term vision, product development, market expansion, and business strategy.**

**Built around the philosophy, “Break up with sugar, not the sweetness,” SORRY SUGAR aims to make zero-added-sugar products more accessible to consumers by offering alternatives that combine indulgent taste with a health-conscious approach.**

**The brand’s products are formulated using monk fruit, a naturally derived sweetener, along with prebiotic fibre, allowing it to deliver beverages and other offerings that cater to changing consumer preferences for healthier everyday consumption.**

> **Palash Arneja, Founder & CEO, SORRY SUGAR said**, “Consumers shouldn’t have to choose between health and taste. That belief sits at the heart of SORRY SUGAR. We want to make zero-added-sugar choices accessible, mainstream and genuinely enjoyable. The opportunity is much larger than a single product or category - we are on a mission to change how India consumes sweetness. Our vision is to build SORRY SUGAR into one of India’s most exciting new-age consumer brands, with the ambition to take it global.”

**The appointment comes as the company prepares for its next stage of expansion, bringing together product innovation, branding, distribution, and business growth under a unified strategy.** SORRY SUGAR currently operates in the flavoured coffee segment, offering a portfolio that is zero added sugar, fibre-rich, and prebiotic.

**Going forward, the company plans to strengthen its presence across both online and offline channels while expanding beyond coffee into additional everyday consumption categories.** The broader goal is to build a consumer platform focused on reducing added sugar consumption without compromising on the flavours and experiences consumers enjoy.

**With increasing awareness around health and nutrition, SORRY SUGAR is positioning itself to capitalize on demand for functional and better-for-you products.** The company’s long-term objective remains centered on transforming consumer habits and creating a new approach to sweetness in everyday diets.

**The brand summed up its ambition with a clear mission: to redefine how India consumes sweetness – by killing the sugar, not the sweetness.**

At-home salon and wellness platform Yes Madam has expanded the availability of its Korean-inspired skincare and haircare brand, Sokora, across direct-to-consumer and e-commerce channels. **The move follows growing consumer demand for the range, which was initially introduced through the company’s professional beauty services.**

**The Sokora portfolio includes products such as Korean Glow Day & Nite Cream, Korean Kera-Tress Shampoo & Conditioner, Korean Reset Glow Face Wash, Sunscreen SPF 50, 5-in-1 Face Serum, and 3-in-1 Hair Serum, among others.** The products are now available through the Yes Madam app, Sokora’s official website, as well as online marketplaces including Amazon, Flipkart, and Myntra.

We have also focused on making the range convenient for everyday use. The strong response to our professional range gave us the confidence to now make Sokora available to consumers for use at home as well.”*

Zigly Pet Care, which describes itself as India’s first omnichannel pet care brand, has acquired Prolife Speciality Vet Clinic in Malad, Mumbai, as part of its strategy to strengthen its veterinary healthcare network and expand its pet care ecosystem across the country.

**The acquisition marks Zigly Pet Care’s third strategic buyout in the veterinary care segment and is expected to support the company’s plans to build a broader network of specialised pet healthcare facilities.** The company said the clinic is expected to transition into a 24x7 facility within the next nine to twelve months.

Established in 2000 and managed by Dr. S. M. As we plan to transform this into a 24x7 facility and integrating it with the Zigly Pet Care ecosystem, we are expanding access to advanced veterinary care while strengthening trusted our ability to deliver a seamless pet parenting experience. This acquisition also reflects our long-term strategy of scaling high-quality veterinary services through strategic partnerships with respected clinicians across the country.”*

**The addition of the Malad-based clinic further strengthens Zigly Pet Care’s veterinary presence in Mumbai and expands its access to specialised pet healthcare services.** The latest acquisition follows the company’s earlier acquisitions of Small Animal Clinic & Surgical Centre in Khar West and Dr. Santa’s Pet Clinic.

According to the company, **these acquisitions are aimed at creating a wider network of veterinary professionals while improving access to consultations, diagnostics, and treatment services for pet owners.** The strategy also seeks to bring specialised veterinary expertise closer to neighbourhood communities and enhance continuity of care for pets requiring long-term medical attention.

![Oziva Posts 80 Pc Revenue Growth in FY26 as HUL Completes Acquisition](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-29T190144.030.jpg)

Oziva, the nutrition and wellness brand now wholly owned by Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), reported strong topline growth in FY26, although rising marketing investments and employee stock option costs weighed on profitability during the fiscal year.

**Oziva’s revenue from operations increased 80 percent to Rs 463.4 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 257.8 crore in FY25.**

**The company derives its revenue from a portfolio of nutrition and wellness products, including plant-based supplements, protein products, vitamins, and solutions focused on skin and hair health.** Product sales remained the sole contributor to operating revenue during the year.

**Domestic sales continued to drive the business, contributing Rs 454 crore in FY26, up from Rs 257 crore in the previous fiscal year.** The company also recorded growth in international markets, where revenue rose to Rs 8.3 crore, compared with Rs 8.3 lakh in FY25.

**Including Rs 4.1 crore generated through non-operating activities, Oziva’s total income stood at Rs 467.5 crore for the fiscal year.**

**On the expenditure side, advertising and promotional spending remained the company’s largest cost component.** Marketing expenditure more than doubled to Rs 246.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 119.8 crore in FY25, accounting for over half of the company’s total expenses.

**The cost of materials consumed increased 63 percent to Rs 116 crore, while employee benefit expenses nearly doubled to Rs 45.4 crore.** This figure included Rs 22 crore in cash-settled employee stock option (ESOP) costs, significantly higher than the Rs 7 crore recorded in the previous year. Transportation and logistics expenses also rose 57 percent to Rs 36.9 crore.

**The increase in spending impacted profitability, resulting in a sharp rise in losses. Oziva reported a net loss of Rs 18.5 crore in FY26,** compared with Rs 4.2 crore in FY25. The company noted that cash-settled ESOP expenses contributed significantly to the loss as employees exercised stock options following changes in ownership. Excluding the Rs 22 crore ESOP-related cost, Oziva would have reported an estimated profit of around Rs 3.5 crore.

**At the end of FY26, the company’s cash and bank balance stood at Rs 8.8 crore, down 67 percent year-on-year, while current assets totaled Rs 106 crore.**

**The financial performance comes ahead of a major ownership transition.** In February 2026, Hindustan Unilever acquired the remaining 49 percent stake in Oziva for Rs 824 crore, making the company a wholly owned subsidiary. **HUL had initially purchased a 51 percent stake in the nutrition brand in December 2022 for Rs 264.28 crore.**

The latest transaction valued Oziva at approximately Rs 1,682 crore, representing a significant increase from the valuation implied during HUL’s initial investment.

Bewakoof, the direct-to-consumer (D2C) fashion and lifestyle brand owned by the Aditya Birla Group, recorded strong revenue growth in FY26, although its losses continued to widen during the fiscal year ended March 2026.

**The company’s operating revenue increased 40.5 percent to Rs 243 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 173 crore in FY25.**

**Known for its range of fashion and lifestyle products, including T-shirts, hoodies, bags, and phone covers, Bewakoof continued to derive the majority of its income from product sales during the year.**

**On the expenditure side, the cost of materials consumed remained the company’s largest expense category.** Material costs rose 45.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 134 crore, up from Rs 92 crore in FY25.

Employee benefit expenses increased 7.7 percent to Rs 28 crore, while marketing and promotional spending grew 26.5 percent to Rs 62 crore, reflecting continued investments in customer acquisition and brand visibility. In contrast, transportation and handling expenses declined 17.1 percent to Rs 29 crore, compared to Rs 35 crore in the previous fiscal year.

The company also reported a significant increase in depreciation expenses, which nearly tripled to Rs 16.6 crore from Rs 6 crore in FY25. Other operating expenses rose 66.1 percent to Rs 66.4 crore, up from Rs 40 crore a year earlier.

Overall, **Bewakoof’s total expenditure climbed 35.5 percent to Rs 336 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 248 crore in the previous fiscal.**

Despite the sharp rise in revenue, **the company reported a wider net loss. Bewakoof’s loss increased 19.4 percent to Rs 87.4 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 73.2 crore in FY25.**

However, some profitability indicators showed improvement. **The company’s EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to Rs 59.8 crore from Rs 60.7 crore in the previous year, while its EBITDA margin improved to -24.6 percent from -35.1 percent.** Its return on capital employed (ROCE) also improved to -63.4 percent, compared with -96.6 percent in FY25.

Operational efficiency improved marginally as well. **Bewakoof spent Rs 1.38 to generate every Rs 1 of operating revenue during FY26, compared with Rs 1.43 in the previous year.**

**The company’s balance sheet reflected moderate growth in assets, with total current** assets rising to Rs 91.1 crore at the end of FY26 from Rs 84.8 crore a year earlier. Cash and bank balances also increased slightly to Rs 22 lakh, compared with Rs 18 lakh in FY25.

**FY26 was also a significant year for the company from a leadership perspective.** Prabhkiran Singh, co-founder of Bewakoof, stepped down from the business in February 2026, ending a 14-year association with the company. His departure came nearly three years after Aditya Birla Digital Fashion Ventures (ABDFVL) acquired a majority stake in Bewakoof in February 2023 through TMRW, the Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first fashion and lifestyle venture.

The Indian Garage Co (TIGC), a direct-to-consumer (D2C) fashion brand focused on men's apparel, recorded a moderate rise in revenue during FY26 amid increasing competition in India's online fashion market. **While the company continued to expand its topline, its losses widened as spending on marketing, operations, and workforce increased during the year.**

**TIGC's revenue from operations grew 15 percent to Rs 234.6 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 204.2 crore in FY25.**

**The company, which designs, manufactures, and sells men's fashion products under its own labels, generated its operating revenue entirely through product sales.**

**Including other income of Rs 2.95 crore, TIGC's total income reached Rs 237.5 crore during FY26, up from Rs 206.9 crore in the previous fiscal year.**

**The company significantly increased its investment in marketing and brand visibility during the year.** Advertising and promotional expenses climbed to Rs 29.3 crore, more than double the Rs 14 crore spent in FY25, reflecting heightened competition among D2C fashion brands.

Job work charges, covering outsourced manufacturing and production activities, stood at Rs 39.5 crore. Employee benefit expenses also increased 24 percent year-on-year to Rs 21 crore.

Additional costs, including depreciation and amortisation, finance charges, legal and professional fees, travel expenditure, and other operational expenses, pushed the company's total spending to Rs 276.1 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 237.5 crore in FY25, representing a 16 percent increase.

As expenses continued to grow faster than revenue, **TIGC's losses widened during the fiscal year.** The company reported a net loss of Rs 28.7 crore, up 27 percent from Rs 22.6 crore in FY25.

**Operational efficiency metrics also reflected the pressure on profitability.** The company spent Rs 1.18 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during FY26, compared with Rs 1.16 in the previous year. Its EBITDA margin improved slightly to -5.12 percent from -6 percent, while return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -12.61 percent.

**TIGC received a major boost in October 2023 when Aditya Birla Group's TMRW invested approximately Rs 155 crore in the business, securing a 51 percent stake.** TMRW has also expanded its presence in the D2C fashion segment through investments in brands such as Bewakoof.

**The company's FY26 performance highlights the evolving dynamics of India's D2C fashion sector, where brands are facing rising customer acquisition costs and increasing competition.**

Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd., the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, and 100Days, has announced senior leadership appointments aimed at strengthening its brand-building and digital commerce functions as the company prepares for its next phase of growth.

**As part of the changes, Varun Gupta, previously Chief Growth Officer, has been elevated to Chief Marketing Officer at Bombay Shaving Company.** The company has also appointed Jasmeet Singh as Senior Vice President, Ecommerce, at Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd.

**The appointments are designed to provide dedicated leadership across two strategic growth areas: consumer brand development and digital commerce expansion.**

**In his new role, Varun Gupta will oversee brand-building initiatives across categories while driving the growth of Bombay Shaving Company and Bombae.** A key part of his mandate will involve strengthening the brands’ direct-to-consumer operations and deepening consumer engagement.

**Gupta has been associated with the company as Chief Growth Officer and Category Head, where he led product innovation and marketing efforts for the trimmers category.** During his tenure, the business expanded significantly, with Bombay Shaving Company becoming the second-largest men’s trimmer brand in India. He also played a key role in scaling the company’s online business while improving profitability. Prior to joining Visage Lines, Gupta held roles at PepsiCo and Hindustan Unilever and was involved in building brands such as Too Yumm! and The Gift Studio for the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group.

> **Varun Gupta, Chief Marketing Officer, Bombay Shaving Company said,** *“The opportunity ahead for Bombay Shaving Company is to build on the strong equity we have created by being bold and defiant of the category and societal codes over the past few years. Consumers have embraced us with open arms and our culture-coded approach is what makes us distinctive. As we scale Bombay Shaving Company and Bombae, the opportunity now is to turbocharge this beyond the top urban centres and build a unified voice that cuts across grooming and other categories and brands. Our focus will be on deepening our consumer connect and sharpening our brand propositions to make them culturally relevant, differentiated and commercially strong. Excited for what’s ahead.”*

**Alongside Gupta’s appointment, Jasmeet Singh will lead the next phase of the company’s ecommerce strategy as Senior Vice President, Ecommerce.** With more than 14 years of experience across ecommerce, D2C, commercial development, and channel sales, Singh brings expertise from leadership roles at L'Oréal, Reckitt, Glanbia Performance Nutrition, and Kenvue.

In his new position, Singh will oversee ecommerce operations across marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, and beauty commerce channels for the company’s portfolio of brands. **His responsibilities will include strengthening channel strategies, identifying new growth opportunities, and driving scale across the digital business.**

> **Jasmeet Singh, Senior Vice President, Ecommerce, Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd. shared,** *"Digital commerce is increasingly shaping how consumers discover, evaluate and purchase personal care products, making it an important growth lever for brands at scale. Visage Lines has a strong and diverse portfolio, with significant opportunities to build greater depth across marketplaces, quick commerce and beauty commerce. My focus will be on creating sharper channel strategies and building win-win propositions for consumers, customers and the brands, with a strong impetus on outside-in learning. We will focus on strengthening the ecommerce ecosystem across the portfolio and building sustainable digital businesses as Visage Lines enters its next phase of growth.”*

**Through brands including Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, and 100Days, Visage Lines has established a presence across men’s grooming, women’s hair removal, and hair styling categories.** Its products are available through D2C channels, ecommerce marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, beauty commerce networks, and offline retail outlets.

Primary healthcare infrastructure company MyRx has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round led by SteerX VC, as the company looks to strengthen its healthcare delivery network and technology capabilities.

According to the company, **the fresh capital will be utilized to expand its clinical network and enhance the technology infrastructure required to make doctor-led primary healthcare services more accessible at scale.**

Founded in 2019 by Sourav Das, Surjit Das, and Neel Rath, MyRx operates a healthcare infrastructure platform that integrates a network of doctors with teleconsultation services, electronic prescriptions, and clinical workflow technology. **The company aims to improve access to primary healthcare through digital healthcare services and a growing ecosystem of healthcare partners.**

**MyRx said it is developing a shared healthcare infrastructure model that connects patients, doctors, and enterprise partners through a unified platform.** By combining clinical expertise with technology-driven consultation allocation, workflow monitoring, and audit systems, the company seeks to help healthcare partners expand patient access while maintaining operational transparency and accountability.

**The Hyderabad-based startup currently handles approximately 35,000 teleconsultations daily and reports 15 percent month-on-month growth.** Its platform brings together doctor availability, teleconsultation services, electronic prescriptions, and workflow management tools, enabling enterprises to integrate healthcare services into their existing offerings.

**As part of its growth strategy, MyRx plans to expand its doctor network, strengthen clinical quality and technology systems, and simplify integration processes for enterprise partners.** The company also intends to further develop its digital clinic model and establish additional healthcare partnerships aimed at connecting remote consultations with local healthcare access points.

**According to MyRx, the platform has achieved a 95th-percentile first doctor-call response time of 30 seconds and a 95th-percentile overall workflow turnaround time of 179 seconds.** The company said these metrics reflect its focus on delivering timely healthcare services while scaling operations.

Sports nutrition brand BigMuscles Nutrition has announced a refresh of its product portfolio, focusing on cleaner ingredients, formulation quality, transparency, and enhanced consumer information. **The company has also introduced a new packaging identity across its range as it responds to changing consumer preferences in the sports nutrition market.**

**The move comes amid growing demand for nutrition products that offer more than just protein content.** Consumers are increasingly paying attention to ingredient quality, sweeteners, digestion and absorption benefits, taste, testing standards and overall product transparency.

**BigMuscles Nutrition has refined the formulation of products such as Premium Gold Whey, which combines Whey Protein Isolate and Whey Protein Concentrate with ingredients including bromelain, stevia, Himalayan salt and cocoa.** The company said bromelain supports protein digestion and absorption, while stevia serves as a plant-based sweetener. **The brand’s product development efforts are supported by its GMP-certified sports nutrition manufacturing facility, which utilizes advanced German technology and multi-stage quality-control processes.** These processes include batch-level testing, contamination screening, and protein-content verification.

BigMuscles Nutrition also highlighted the use of Bruker TANGO FT NIR technology, a German analytical system that helps assess key product parameters and supports the verification of protein content accuracy.

**Alongside product enhancements, the company has unveiled refreshed packaging across its portfolio.** The updated design features a cleaner visual identity and places greater emphasis on ingredient and product information, making it easier for consumers to understand what they are purchasing.

> **Jitika Gupta, Co-founder and CMO, BigMuscles Nutrition said,** *“The consumer today is not just asking how much protein is in a product, but what is in it, how it is made and whether they can trust what is on the label. That is changing the category. Our evolution is rooted in responding to that consumer with cleaner formulations, greater transparency and stronger quality processes. The new packaging brings this thinking to the forefront, making the information consumers care about easier to see and understand. It is a step towards building a more transparent, informed and consumer-first nutrition brand.”*

**The refreshed portfolio includes products such as Premium Gold Whey, Gold Whey Isolate and Nitra Isolate, catering to a range of fitness and nutritional requirements.** Through these changes, BigMuscles Nutrition aims to strengthen its focus on ingredient quality, transparency, taste consistency and manufacturing standards as consumer expectations continue to evolve in the sports nutrition category.

![D2C Personal Care Brand Phitku Launches Mouth Paste in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-23T122935.531.jpg)

Personal care brand Phitku has entered the oral care segment with the launch of Phitku Mouth Paste, marking the company's expansion beyond its existing deodorant portfolio. **The new product extends the brand’s core philosophy of “Eliminate. Don’t Mask.”** into the oral hygiene category, with a focus on addressing breath odour at its source.

Positioned as a whole-mouth oral care product, Phitku Mouth Paste is designed to support care across the teeth, gums and tongue rather than focusing solely on dental cleaning. **The company said the formulation aims to address oral freshness and odour management through a broader approach to everyday oral hygiene.**

**A key ingredient in the formulation is Phitkari (Potassium Alum), which has been a central component of the brand’s deodorant products.**

**The formulation combines Phitkari (Potassium Alum), Red Banana, Neem and Clove, alongside hydrated silica for cleaning and surface stain removal.** Phitku said the product has been developed around three core oral care areas—teeth, gums and tongue—with particular attention to managing odour-causing bacteria that can accumulate on the tongue.

> **Rahul Dokania, Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Phitku said,** “Developing Mouth Paste was about translating Phitku’s odour-first philosophy into a completely new category while staying true to what the brand stands for. We looked at oral care beyond just the teeth and focused on bringing together ingredients such as Phitkari, Red Banana, Neem and Clove in a formulation designed around the teeth, gums and tongue. The intent was to create an everyday oral-care product that approaches breath odour differently, rather than simply adding another toothpaste to the shelf.”

> **Neha Marda, Co-founder, Phitku shared,** “We have always believed that personal care should address the source of a concern rather than simply mask it. With Mouth Paste, we wanted to take that philosophy into a category where the conversation has traditionally centred around teeth. Your mouth is more than your teeth, and we believe your oral care should be too. Mouth Paste is our way of encouraging consumers to think about oral care more holistically.”

> **Sumit Marda, Co-founder & CEO, Phitku stated,**, “For us, entering oral care was never about becoming another toothpaste brand. We saw an opportunity to take what Phitku already stands for odour management and apply that thinking to breath odour. Mouth Paste is an extension of our brand philosophy, but it also challenges consumers to question whether we have been thinking about oral care too narrowly.”

**Phitku Mouth Paste is SLS-free and fluoride-free and is positioned as an odour-focused oral care solution rather than a conventional toothpaste.** The launch follows the success of the brand’s Alum Crystal Roll-On range and reflects its strategy of expanding into adjacent hygiene categories.

Founded on January 16, 2025, by Neha Marda, Sumit Marda and Rahul Dokania, Phitku focuses on developing personal care products built around functional ingredients and modern formulations. **The new Mouth Paste, available in a pack of two, has been on sale through the brand’s website since August 16, 2026.**

![NEWME Expands to 40 Stores Across India, Targets 60 Outlets by March 2027](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-22T181508.628.jpg)

Gen Z-focused fashion-tech brand NEWME has expanded its retail footprint to 40 stores across India following the launch of two new outlets in Lajpat Nagar, Delhi, and Model Town, Jalandhar.

The latest openings mark a significant milestone in the company’s offline growth strategy. **NEWME has added 22 stores in 2026 alone, surpassing the 18 stores it opened during its first three years of operations.** The brand is now aiming to reach 50 stores by December 2026 and 60 stores by March 2027.

> **Sumit Jasoria, CEO & Co-founder, NEWME said,** “Reaching 40 stores is an important milestone for us, but the pace behind it is even more significant. In our first three years, we were deliberately measured about retail expansion, using our early stores to understand consumer behaviour, markets and the right formats for NEWME. The traction we have seen has given us the confidence to accelerate, and we have now added 22 stores this year alone—more than in our first three years. We are now looking to reach 50 stores by December and 60 stores by March 2027, as we build a strong physical network that takes NEWME closer to young consumers across the country. We believe India has the consumers, talent, and opportunity to build a global fashion company, and the next generation of Indian brands can make that happen.”

**As part of its expansion strategy, NEWME has entered emerging markets such as Jalandhar, Jodhpur, Ludhiana, Visakhapatnam, and Vadodara, while further strengthening its presence in key markets including Delhi, Mumbai, and Rajasthan.**

**In August, the company launched five new stores across Delhi, Mumbai, and Rajasthan.** Its retail growth strategy spans both shopping malls and high-street locations, focusing on established retail destinations as well as developing catchment areas with strong demand from young shoppers.

**Decisions on store locations are driven by factors such as digital demand, consumer behavior insights, market potential, and local traction.** The brand leverages data from its online platform to identify markets where physical stores can enhance customer engagement and brand visibility.

**Offline retail has become an increasingly important part of NEWME’s business, currently accounting for more than 30 percent of overall revenue.** The company reported that its offline segment has recorded 100 percent year-on-year growth and expects its contribution to rise further as the store network expands.

**Supporting its omnichannel strategy is NEWME Zip, the brand’s quick-fashion delivery model, which works alongside its e-commerce platform and physical stores.** The company continues to focus on combining trend-driven fashion with faster fulfillment and convenience for consumers.

Founded in 2022, NEWME has served more than 35 lakh customers and operates with a business model built around trend intelligence, technology, creator partnerships, and community-led engagement tailored to Gen Z shoppers.

![Kitchen Appliances Brand Wonderchef Targets Rs 600 Cr Sales in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-19T110845.713.jpg)

Kitchen and home appliances brand Wonderchef is aiming for net sales of Rs 600 crore in the current financial year, up from Rs 486 crore last year and Rs 426 crore in the previous fiscal year, as it strengthens its omnichannel presence and expands across digital commerce platforms.

**The company expects digital channels to account for 50 percent of its total sales over the next five years, compared to nearly 35 percent at present.** Founder and CEO Ravi Saxena said the contribution of digital sales has increased from around 25 percent to 35 percent over the last two to two-and-a-half years, supported by a growing base of young consumers furnishing their first homes and increasingly preferring online shopping.

**According to Saxena, digital sales are projected to grow at nearly twice the pace of general trade and modern trade channels.** As a result, e-commerce, quick commerce, and omnichannel retail are becoming key pillars of Wonderchef’s growth strategy.

**The company is targeting overall growth of 27 percent this year and expects festive season sales to rise by nearly 30 percent compared to the previous year.** Currently, Wonderchef is growing at approximately 20 percent year-on-year through internal accruals and has no immediate plans to seek external funding. **EBITDA profitability remains in the single-digit range as the company continues investing in expansion initiatives.**

Wonderchef’s distribution network spans nearly 23,000 to 24,000 retail touchpoints across India, including general trade, modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce platforms, army and police canteens, exclusive brand outlets, corporate gifting channels, exports, and its women entrepreneur network.

**Its offline presence includes around 14,000 general trade outlets, 2,000 modern trade stores, 4,000 army and police canteen points, and 30 exclusive brand outlets.** During the current financial year, the company plans to open 12 additional stores, split evenly between company-owned and franchise-operated formats. Each outlet typically covers 500–600 sq ft and requires an investment of around Rs 30–40 lakh.

**The company’s smart appliance range, especially the Magic series, has emerged as a significant growth contributor.** The portfolio includes products such as Chef Magic, Chai Magic, and Roti Magic.

The at-home coffee segment is also gaining traction. **Wonderchef said it sold approximately 1.5 lakh domestic coffee machines in India last year and currently offers 16–17 products in this category.**

In cookware, consumer preferences are shifting toward premium materials, with nearly 50 percent of sales now coming from triply steel and ceramic cookware alongside conventional non-stick products. **The company recently introduced a vegetarian air fryer bundled with a 100-recipe cookbook, with its initial inventory selling out during the pre-booking phase.**

International business currently contributes less than 2 percent of Wonderchef’s overall revenue, despite the brand having distribution partnerships across nearly 15 countries, indicating significant room for future global expansion.

D2C kitchen and bathware fittings brand Ruhe India has announced plans to significantly expand its offline retail presence, aiming to increase its network from 9 exclusive stores to 50 outlets over the next 12 months. **The announcement coincides with the company’s sixth anniversary and reflects its broader strategy to strengthen its footprint across India.**

**The company said its offline business has become an important growth driver, complementing its digital-first approach by enhancing customer engagement, product discovery, and market reach.** Supported by its expansion plans, Ruhe is targeting Rs 500 crore in revenue over the next three financial years, backed by a reported 90 percent compound annual growth rate (CAGR).

**To support its retail growth, Ruhe is leveraging a zero-inventory retail model, under which products are supplied to dealers from local warehouses within four hours, reducing the need for dealers to maintain large inventories.** The company plans to use this model to expand across metropolitan cities as well as Tier I and Tier II markets.

**Ruhe’s stores are designed around a boutique-style shopping experience, allowing homeowners, architects, and interior designers to interact with products before making purchasing decisions.** The company said the format is intended to help customers assess product dimensions, materials, and water-flow functionality, reducing issues related to fitment and installation.

> **Kapil Gupta, Founder and Director, Ruhe India said**, “For years, kitchen and bathroom fittings were bought through fragmented dealer networks, often leaving homeowners with severe fitment issues and uncertain quality. Our exclusive stores bridge digital convenience with hands-on product validation, while our zero-inventory model addresses partners’ working capital challenges. With retail contributing nearly a third of revenues and initial outlets breaking even in under six months, expanding to 50 stores in the next 12 months is a natural step. With a 90 percent CAGR and a target of Rs 500 crore in revenue over the next three financial years, we are seeing strong market demand and building a solid foundation for our long-term growth.”

**The company said its strategy combines the reach of a digital-first business with the benefits of physical retail, enabling consumers to experience products firsthand while maintaining efficient supply chain operations.**

With plans to expand from 9 to 50 stores, Ruhe India is looking to strengthen its position in the kitchen and bathware fittings market by creating a wider retail network and improving accessibility for consumers across key markets in India.

Non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (RTD) and mixer brand Twisted Tails, owned by RAD Beverages, has expanded its distribution network with a launch on Swiggy Instamart across Mumbai and Bengaluru. **The move marks the brand’s entry into quick commerce in the two metro markets and is aimed at increasing accessibility for consumers seeking on-demand beverage options.**

**The company said the launch strengthens its omnichannel strategy by making its portfolio available for delivery within minutes through the quick commerce platform.**

**Built around the theme “One for Every Tale,” Twisted Tails offers a range of non-alcoholic beverages developed using real fruit juices and spices, with lower added sugar and no artificial flavouring.** The brand positions each variant around a distinct flavour profile and consumer occasion, catering to social gatherings, celebrations, and individual consumption moments.

**The expansion comes as consumer demand grows for premium mixers and non-alcoholic beverages that offer unique flavour experiences and convenience.** Quick commerce has emerged as a key channel for beverage discovery, particularly among urban consumers seeking instant access to products for home consumption and social occasions.

**Twisted Tails currently offers four 250 ml variants priced at Rs 200 each: BIZZARE (Orange & Coffee), MYSTICAL (Vanilla & Caramel), ENIGMATIC (Tea & Jasmine), and UNCANNY (Apricot, Peach, Cinnamon & Clove).** According to the company, each product combines familiar ingredients with unconventional pairings to create distinctive flavour experiences.

> **Radhika Sharda, Co-Founder, RAD Beverages said**, "Consumers today think about beverages very differently. They are more curious, discerning, intentional and experimental than ever before. They are looking beyond conventional choices for distinctive flavour experiences, quality ingredients and the flexibility to enjoy beverages in ways that suit their moments and occasions. This insight is what Twisted Tails was built around. Every flavour is designed to evoke an emotion and offer a unique experience while giving consumers the option to enjoy it their way. With the Swiggy Instamart launch in Mumbai and Bengaluru, we can now elevate and be part of these moments more instantly and conveniently than ever before."

> **Atin Khanna, Co-Founder, RAD Beverages added**, "For us, flavour creation goes beyond simply combining ingredients. Every Twisted Tails variant is crafted to deliver a complete sensory experience through taste, aroma, texture and storytelling. Built using real fruit juices, real spices and unexpected flavour pairings, the portfolio is designed to surprise, delight and adapt effortlessly to different occasions and drinking preferences. Our launch on Swiggy Instamart makes it easier than ever for consumers in Mumbai and Bengaluru to access these flavour experiences on demand."

> **Raghav Sharda, Co-Founder, RAD Beverages said**, "Mumbai and Bengaluru are two of India's most exciting cities for food, beverage and lifestyle trends, making them important markets for Twisted Tails. Getting onto Swiggy Instamart is a huge step for our omnichannel growth strategy. It means people in Mumbai and Bengaluru can now grab a Twisted Tails exactly when the craving hits. As we scale, our main goal is simply making it easier for everyone to find and enjoy our drinks."

**In addition to Swiggy Instamart, Twisted Tails is available on Blinkit, at Le Marché stores in Delhi, Nature’s Basket outlets across Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Kolkata, as well as through online marketplaces including Amazon and Flipkart, alongside the brand’s direct-to-consumer website.**

![Healthcare Platform Practo Elevates Shashank ND Singh to Managing Director and Executive Chairman](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-17T152453.356.jpg)

Healthcare technology platform Practo has unveiled a new leadership structure as it prepares for its next phase of growth and international expansion. **Under the revised framework, Founder and CEO Shashank ND Singh has been elevated to the role of Managing Director and Executive Chairman, while Jagnoor Singh, previously the company’s Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective September 1, 2026.**

**In his new role as Executive Chairman, Shashank ND Singh will continue to guide Practo’s long-term vision, product direction, and overall strategy.** He will also focus on areas such as innovation, capital allocation, corporate development, and potential inorganic growth opportunities.

**Jagnoor Singh, who joined Practo as COO in January 2025, has been instrumental in driving the company’s growth initiatives and expansion into new markets.** Prior to joining Practo, he held leadership positions at Bharti Airtel, Unacademy, and OYO. As CEO, he will be responsible for leading the company’s business strategy, operations, and growth across global markets.

**Alongside the leadership transition, Practo has expanded the responsibilities of several senior executives and co-founders.**

**Siddhartha Nihalani, co-founder of Practo, has been appointed Chief Operating Officer – B2C,** where he will oversee the company’s consumer-facing business operations. Meanwhile, **Rowel Coelho, who previously led monetization efforts, has taken on the role of Chief Operating Officer – B2B**, focusing on the company’s enterprise and healthcare provider business.

**Additionally, Abhinav Lal, co-founder of Practo, has been named Chief Scientist and will spearhead the company’s artificial intelligence research initiatives and healthcare-focused partnerships.**

The leadership overhaul comes at a time when Practo is expanding its consumer healthcare platform into international markets, including the United Arab Emirates and the United States.

**Practo has maintained strong business momentum, reporting 40 percent year-on-year growth while remaining profitable for the past two and a half years.**

**Practo currently connects patients with more than 700,000 doctors and healthcare providers worldwide through its healthcare platform.** The company also operates Insta, its hospital and clinic management solution, which is used across 1,200 healthcare facilities.

The leadership changes are expected to support Practo’s expansion strategy and strengthen its focus on innovation, technology, and global healthcare services as the company scales its operations across multiple markets.

![RentoMojo Lists at Rs 482.45 on NSE, Surges Nearly 19 Pc on Debut](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-17T131038.138.jpg)

RentoMojo, the furniture and appliance rental platform, made a strong debut on the stock exchanges, with its shares listing at a premium of nearly 19 percent over the initial public offering (IPO) price.

**On the NSE, the stock opened at Rs 482.45 per share, representing a 19.42 percent premium to its issue price of Rs 404. On the BSE, the company’s shares debuted at Rs 480, up 18.81 percent from the IPO price.**

Investor interest continued after listing, pushing the stock to an intraday high of Rs 500 on the BSE. At around 10:10 AM IST, the stock was trading at Rs 500, reflecting a 23.76 percent gain over the issue price and a 4.15 percent rise from its opening level on the BSE. The company’s market capitalization stood at approximately Rs 5,205.74 crore.

**The market valuation at listing was around 30 percent higher than the valuation of nearly Rs 4,006 crore that the company sought at the upper end of its IPO price band of Rs 384–404 per share.**

**The strong market debut followed robust investor participation in RentoMojo’s Rs 1,256 crore IPO, which closed with an overall subscription of 72.88 times.**

**Ahead of the public issue, the company had raised Rs 376.1 crore from 41 anchor investors through the allotment of 93.1 lakh shares at Rs 404 apiece.**

The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.74 crore shares, aggregating Rs 1,105.6 crore.

**Geetansh Bamania, Co-founder and CEO of RentoMojo, received Rs 34.31 crore through the sale of 8.49 lakh shares.** Other shareholders, including Rajeev Chitrabhanu HUF and Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain, also recorded significant returns on the shares sold through the OFS.

**Following the IPO, investors such as Accel, Edelweiss, and ValueQuest continue to hold substantial stakes in the company, while IDG Ventures India Fund III, GMO Payment Gateway, GMO GFF, and some other shareholders exited their investments completely.**

Founded in 2014 by Geetansh Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a subscription-based platform that allows consumers to rent furniture, home appliances, and household products.

**As of March 2026, the company reported approximately 2.5 lakh active subscribers and a portfolio of 8.5 lakh live rental items across its product categories.**

**Financially, the company delivered strong growth in FY26.** Operating revenue increased 45.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 387 crore, compared to Rs 266 crore in the previous fiscal. Profit after tax rose nearly 142 percent to Rs 104.3 crore, supported in part by a tax credit of Rs 36.6 crore.

**RentoMojo’s EBITDA grew 38 percent year-on-year to Rs 163.5 crore during FY26, although the EBITDA margin narrowed to 41.5 percent from 43.6 percent a year earlier.** The company generated nearly Rs 170 crore in operating cash flow while investing around Rs 175 crore in capital expenditure to expand its rental inventory.

Sustainable footwear brand Neeman’s has set a target of achieving Rs 1,000 crore in revenue within the next three years, supported by an aggressive retail expansion strategy that includes building a network of 500 stores across India.

**The company reported revenue of more than Rs 185 crore in the previous financial year and expects to close the current fiscal year at around Rs 350 crore by March 2027.** As it enters its next phase of growth, Neeman’s is increasing its focus on offline retail while continuing to strengthen its digital-first business model.

**The planned store rollout is aimed at expanding the brand’s reach across the country and improving consumer access to its products and in-store experience.** Through this expansion, Neeman’s seeks to evolve from a digitally driven footwear brand into a larger national retail player.

> **Taran Chhabra, Co-founder & CEO, Neeman’s** **said**, **“**We have always believed that footwear is a deeply personal and everyday category, and that there is an opportunity to redefine what consumers expect from their shoes. Our focus has been to build products that people genuinely love — combining exceptional comfort with great design, versatility and value. Today, Neeman’s is innovating and on course to close this year at Rs 350 crore in revenue. This gives us the confidence to think much bigger. As we build towards Rs 1,000 crore, our ambition is not simply to grow the business, but to build a distinctive Indian footwear brand that earns a place in the everyday lives of millions of consumers.”

The company stated that comfort will continue to be a core element of its product strategy as it competes in the growing footwear market. **Neeman’s designs its products for daily wear across multiple occasions, including work, travel, and everyday activities.**

> **Amar Preet Singh, Co-founder & COO, Neeman’s shared**, “The ₹1,000 crore ambition represents a very different scale of business, and getting there will require us to build the right foundation across every part of the organisation. From strengthening our product engine and supply chain to investing in technology, retail and execution, we are focused on creating the capabilities that can sustain long-term growth. The 500-store expansion is an important part of that transformation, because it gives us the opportunity to take the Neeman’s experience to consumers across the country while building a stronger national footprint.”

**As part of its growth strategy, Neeman’s plans to increase market penetration, expand its product offerings, and invest further in technology, supply chain infrastructure, and retail operations.** The company believes these initiatives will play a key role in supporting its long-term revenue goals and strengthening its position in India’s footwear industry.

![ORIGEM Launches Flexible Jewellery Upgrade Programme for Consumers](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T134550.999.jpg)

Lab-grown diamond jewellery brand ORIGEM, backed by Goldiam International Limited, has launched a new 110 percent Lifetime Exchange Value proposition, aimed at offering customers greater flexibility and long-term value on their jewellery purchases.

**The initiative comes as consumer preferences continue to evolve, with buyers increasingly seeking products that align with changing lifestyles, personal style choices, and long-term value considerations.** Through the programme, ORIGEM is seeking to redefine the ownership experience within the diamond jewellery segment by enabling customers to exchange their jewellery over time rather than viewing it as a one-time purchase.

**Under the new proposition, customers will receive 110 percent exchange value on the diamond component of their ORIGEM jewellery for life.** In addition, the company is offering 100 percent exchange value on the gold component at prevailing gold rates, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

The programme is designed to provide consumers with the flexibility to upgrade or exchange jewellery for different designs, commemorate personal milestones, or select pieces that better reflect their current preferences. **The initiative is intended to make jewellery ownership more adaptable while rewarding customers for remaining within the ORIGEM ecosystem.**

> **Anmol Bhansali, Managing Director, Goldiam International Limited said**, “The jewellery category has traditionally been built around the idea of permanence, but the consumer is changing. Today, personal style is far more fluid, and people want their purchases to work with the way they live and evolve. With ORIGEM’s 110 percent Lifetime Exchange Value, we are bringing that thinking into jewellery - giving consumers an added sense of confidence & financial security that their choice today will continue to hold value tomorrow. It is a step towards making the category more relevant to how consumers actually think and shop today. This is increasingly relevant in the lab grown diamond space, where we hope to encourage our customers to experiment frequently across a much larger variety of shapes than is otherwise affordable with natural diamonds.”

**The company believes the initiative reflects a broader shift in consumer expectations, where buyers are increasingly looking for flexibility and value retention beyond the initial transaction.**

> **Abhinav Kumar, President, ORIGEM shared,** “We believe the first purchase should be the beginning of the jewellery journey, not the end of it. Consumers should have the freedom to discover different designs and make new choices without feeling restricted by an earlier purchase. Our lifetime exchange programme is built to enable exactly that, to not just allow, but also to reward upgrading one’s jewellery while making the overall experience of owning Origem diamond jewellery more contemporary and consumer-friendly.”

**The launch also highlights ORIGEM’s efforts to differentiate itself in the growing lab-grown diamond jewellery market by focusing on post-purchase value and customer experience.** The company said the initiative broadens the conversation around jewellery ownership by emphasizing long-term utility and flexibility in addition to the emotional significance of the purchase.
