![SKINQ Combines D2C and Offline Retail to Scale Skincare Business in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T125157.347.jpg)

Dermatologist-led skincare brand SKINQ is sharpening its growth strategy in India by combining evidence-based formulations, consumer education, and an omnichannel retail approach. **The company is positioning itself as a specialized skincare brand focused on the needs of Indian and melanin-rich skin, targeting concerns such as pigmentation, sensitivity, inflammation, acne, skin-barrier repair, and sun exposure.**

**Co-founded by Ashish Mishra, SKINQ is responding to a growing shift in consumer behavior, where buyers are increasingly paying attention to ingredients, product efficacy, and the scientific research behind skincare formulations.** Rather than opting for trend-driven products, consumers are seeking personalized solutions tailored to their individual skin concerns.

According to Mishra, the brand was founded on the belief that skincare should be guided by what the skin genuinely requires instead of following market trends or relying on excessive ingredients.

**At the core of SKINQ’s product development strategy is its “Proof over promise” philosophy.** The company emphasizes measurable and verifiable product claims, using dermatological expertise and scientific validation to build trust among consumers. This focus on evidence-backed skincare comes as transparency, clinical testing, and formulation credibility become increasingly important purchase drivers in India’s evolving beauty and personal care market.

The Indian skincare sector has become highly competitive, with direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, global beauty companies, and pharmacy-led skincare players all competing for a growing base of informed consumers. In this environment, brands that can demonstrate efficacy and ingredient transparency are gaining greater attention.

**SKINQ believes there is a significant opportunity in developing products specifically designed for Indian and melanin-rich skin.** The company notes that skincare has traditionally been approached through a broad, one-size-fits-all lens, despite the unique challenges faced by different skin tones and types. Concerns such as pigmentation, inflammation, and prolonged sun exposure often affect melanin-rich skin differently, creating demand for targeted solutions that prioritize long-term skin health rather than purely cosmetic outcomes.

**To build awareness and engage directly with customers, SKINQ has leveraged its D2C platform and social media channels.** These platforms have enabled the company to educate consumers about skincare science while also gathering valuable feedback on product performance and customer preferences.

![EV Mobility Startup Bounce Partners with ONDC to Scale Delivery Network](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-14T162422.212.jpg)

Electric mobility company Bounce has announced a partnership with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to support the growth of India’s open logistics ecosystem through sustainable, electric vehicle-driven last-mile delivery services.

**The collaboration comes as ONDC continues to expand its logistics network, which currently includes more than 50 logistics service providers, over 60,000 merchants, 150,000 delivery partners, and facilitates upwards of 12,000 deliveries every day through its interoperable digital infrastructure.**

Under the partnership, Bounce will combine its electric mobility and fleet management capabilities with ONDC’s Open Delivery Protocol (ODP) to create a more efficient, scalable, and inclusive logistics ecosystem. **The initiative is expected to help merchants, brands, and logistics providers of different sizes participate more seamlessly in digital commerce.**

**India’s logistics sector remains one of the largest globally, but fragmentation continues to present challenges for businesses seeking dependable third-party delivery solutions at scale.** At the same time, smaller fleet operators often face limitations in accessing technology platforms and consistent delivery demand.

**ONDC’s Open Delivery Protocol has been developed to address these challenges by enabling merchants to connect with multiple logistics providers through a single integration.** The framework allows national logistics companies, regional operators, and independent fleet owners to compete on a common digital infrastructure, reducing integration complexities and improving operational efficiency.

The platform also incorporates features such as intelligent rider allocation and First-In-First-Out (FIFO) order matching, designed to enhance delivery performance, improve fleet utilization, and create additional earning opportunities for delivery partners.

**Unlike traditional logistics operators, Bounce manages both vehicle production and fleet operations in-house, enabling greater control over vehicle performance, utilization, and operating costs throughout the delivery process.**

> **Rohit Lohia, Chief Operating Officer, ONDC** **said,** *“Neither merchants nor logistics providers should have to go through cumbersome one-on-one integrations. ONDC's Open Delivery Protocol allows businesses to integrate once and access a growing network of logistics providers through common digital infrastructure. Similarly logistics players get access to demand with a single simple integration. Today, more than 60,000 merchants and over 150,000 delivery partners are already leveraging this ecosystem. Partnerships like Bounce further strengthen the network by bringing more logistics capacity, better fleet utilisation and greater choice for businesses across India.”*

> **Vivekananda Hallekere, CEO and Co-founder, Bounce shared**, *“We've built deep muscle in running complex fleet operations at scale, and now that we manufacture in-house, those two capabilities compound. Everything we do comes down to two things for the rider: put them on a great scooter, and help them earn the best. ONDC gives that capability open rails to run on. Instead of locking our riders inside a walled garden, we plug an entire manufacturer-to-gig-worker operation into an open network, and the fulfilment speed we're seeing is what happens when fleet expertise meets in-house manufacturing on open commerce.”*

**Bounce currently supports more than 12,000 riders across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai and the National Capital Region through its platform.** The company expects this rider network to expand significantly over the coming year as demand for EV-powered delivery services grows.

![Zigly Strengthens Preventive Pet Healthcare with New Annual Dog Care Packages](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T174935.430.jpg)

Zigly Pet Care, an omnichannel pet care brand in India, has introduced a new range of annual dog health packages tailored to different life stages as part of its fifth anniversary celebrations. **The plans, designed for puppies, adult dogs and senior dogs, aim to simplify preventive healthcare by combining veterinary, diagnostic and grooming services under a single annual package.**

**The launch reflects the company’s focus on encouraging structured and proactive pet care at a time when more pet owners are becoming increasingly involved in the health and well-being of their animals.** According to Zigly, many pet parents continue to face challenges in keeping track of routine healthcare requirements such as vaccinations, deworming schedules, and regular health assessments when these services are managed separately.

**The newly introduced plans are intended to streamline these requirements by bringing together essential healthcare and wellness services based on a dog’s age and needs.**

**The Puppy Care package, priced at Rs 17,000, includes vaccinations, deworming, a baseline blood panel, diet and nutrition consultation, grooming services, and unlimited veterinary consultations.**

**The Adult Care package is available at Rs 20,000 and covers annual vaccinations, deworming, blood and urine tests, a chest X-ray, dental examination, grooming services, five nights of boarding, and unlimited vet consultations.**

**For older pets, the Senior Care package has been priced at Rs 30,000. T**he plan includes biannual blood and urine tests, ECG and blood pressure monitoring, joint and bone examinations, seven nights of boarding, home sample collection and unlimited veterinary consultations.

> **Saurabh Jain, CEO, Zigly Pet Care, said,** *“Completing five years is an important milestone for us, but what matters more is what we have learnt from being part of pet parents’ everyday lives. While pet parents often want to do the right things for their pets, they face challenges in keeping track of everything throughout the year and knowing when something needs attention. We wanted to make that process simpler. These health packages bring important aspects of care into one plan and give pet parents the flexibility to consult a vet whenever they need to. For us, the initiative is about making regular care easier to follow, rather than waiting for a health concern to become urgent.”*

**A common feature across all three plans is unlimited veterinary consultations, aimed at providing easier access to professional guidance throughout the year.** The company believes this will help pet parents address concerns related to changes in behaviour, appetite, activity levels or overall health before they develop into more serious issues.

**To improve affordability and accessibility, Zigly has also introduced flexible payment options, allowing customers to pay for the packages over three, six or twelve months.**

As part of its fifth anniversary celebrations, the company’s social impact initiative, Zigly Foundation, is organizing feeding drives in Gurgaon and Noida. The foundation plans to distribute 200 kilograms of nutritious food at each location for community dogs, promoting responsible and compassionate care for stray animals.

Recode Studios Limited has strengthened its omnichannel retail strategy by entering the quick-commerce segment through Nykaa Now, Nykaa’s 60-minute delivery service. **The move will make the company’s beauty and personal care products available to consumers across seven major cities, enabling faster access to its portfolio through rapid delivery.**

**The expansion builds on Recode’s existing presence on Nykaa’s platform, where the brand has gained traction among beauty shoppers.** By joining Nykaa Now, Recode aims to enhance product accessibility while benefiting from an additional consumer touchpoint within the fast-growing quick-commerce ecosystem.

According to the company, **the partnership is expected to improve product discovery and convenience for consumers, particularly in urban markets where demand for faster delivery services continues to rise.**

**A key aspect of the initiative is that Recode’s entry into quick commerce does not require additional investment.** The company said it will leverage the supply chain and fulfilment infrastructure already established through its existing relationship with Nykaa, allowing it to scale its presence on Nykaa Now without incremental spending on logistics or infrastructure.

**In addition to its quick-commerce expansion, Recode Studios has also strengthened its distribution footprint through Nykaa Superstore, the beauty retailer’s B2B platform.** The company expects this channel to support deeper penetration into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets by connecting with regional retailers and increasing product availability beyond metropolitan cities.

The presence on Nykaa Superstore is also expected to enhance Recode’s offline retail reach by providing access to Nykaa’s established business-to-business distribution network.

> **Dheeraj Bansal, Chairman & Managing Director, Recode Studios said,** “Our focus is to build a wider and more diversified omnichannel distribution network while remaining disciplined on capital deployment and spending. From an established base of omnichannel sales network in FY26, we are expanding our consumer touchpoints across B2B distribution, modern trade, premium kiosks and quick commerce. Our presence on platforms such as Nykaa, Nykaa Superstore and Nykaa Now allows us to leverage established digital, fulfilment and distribution infrastructure without requiring incremental investment in logistics for the quick-commerce channel. At the same time, partnerships with modern trade formats such as NewU and the rollout of premium kiosks are expected to strengthen our physical presence. This expansion is aimed at improving product accessibility across metro as well as Tier II and Tier III markets, increasing consumer touchpoints and strengthening brand visibility. Supported by this broader distribution network, management is targeting revenue growth of around 50% as it scales the business across FY27 and beyond.Our strategy remains focused on achieving this growth through discipline execution, wider market access and a capital-efficient omnichannel model.”

**The latest expansion reflects Recode Studios’ broader strategy of building a diversified distribution network across online and offline channels.** By combining quick commerce, B2B distribution, modern trade partnerships and physical retail formats, the company aims to strengthen brand visibility and improve accessibility for consumers across different regions of India.

Korean skincare brand The Face Shop has unveiled a refreshed look for its bestselling Rice Water Bright Foaming Cleanser, introducing new packaging while retaining the original formula that has made the product a longstanding favourite among consumers worldwide.

**The packaging makeover gives the cleanser a more contemporary and visually appealing identity, aligning with evolving beauty aesthetics while preserving the product’s core attributes.** The company said the revamp is aimed at celebrating a skincare staple that has continued to resonate with consumers across generations and changing beauty trends.

**Known for its rich foaming texture and gentle cleansing performance, the Rice Water Bright Foaming Cleanser is formulated with Korean rice extract sourced from Yeoju, a region recognised for producing premium-quality rice.**

According to the brand, **the cleanser removes 99.9 percent of pore impurities and helps enhance skin brightness after a single wash.** While the packaging has been updated, consumers can expect the same formula, texture, product size, and price point that they have come to associate with the cleanser over the years.

> **Aashriya Sharma, Head of Marketing, The Face Shop said,** “Rice Water Bright Foaming Cleanser, has been a much-loved part of skincare routines for years, and its cult status comes from the trust consumers have placed in the formula. With this packaging refresh, we wanted to give an iconic favourite a fresh, contemporary identity while staying true to what consumers already love. This is our way of celebrating an icon that continues to be relevant, loved and timeless, while staying true to everything that has made it a skincare favourite ”

**The Rice Water Bright Foaming Cleanser has sold more than 47 million units globally, establishing a strong presence in the rice water cleanser category.** The product’s popularity is supported by nearly two decades of research into rice-based skincare ingredients, reflecting The Face Shop’s long-term focus on developing formulations centred around clear, fresh-looking skin.

**The company highlighted that 100 percent of users reported satisfaction with skin radiance and hydration after using the product.** The brand also continues to invest in rice-focused skincare research, reinforcing its expertise in one of beauty’s most widely used natural ingredients.

**With the packaging refresh, The Face Shop aims to bring renewed attention to one of its most recognisable products while maintaining the qualities that have helped it build a loyal consumer base worldwide.** The updated design marks a new chapter for the Rice Water Bright Foaming Cleanser, balancing modern appeal with the legacy that has defined the product for years.

Ergonomic comfort and wellness brand Frido has expanded its offline footprint in the National Capital Region with the launch of a new experience store at Vegas Mall, Sector 14, Dwarka, New Delhi. **The move is part of the company’s broader strategy to strengthen its physical retail presence and provide consumers with a hands-on experience of its growing portfolio of wellness and comfort-focused products.**

Swiggy has entered into a partnership with Hero MotoCorp to provide delivery partners associated with its Food Marketplace and Instamart businesses with access to two-wheelers, financing facilities, and road safety training.

As part of the tie-up, Swiggy delivery partners will be able to choose from eligible Hero MotoCorp two-wheeler models through the Swiggy app and avail of exclusive pricing at participating Hero dealerships. **The programme will also offer financing options of up to 90% loan-to-value, along with competitive interest rates.**

T**he collaboration extends beyond vehicle access, with Hero MotoCorp also offering road safety training to Swiggy riders through its Ride Safe India CSR initiative.** The programme will include a combination of digital modules and instructor-led sessions covering preventive riding practices, hazard identification, traffic regulations, responsible riding, and emergency response.

**The two companies marked the partnership with a road safety training programme held at Hero MotoCorp’s Traffic Training Park in Gurugram.** Participating delivery partners were provided with safety kits containing a full-face helmet, medical kit, certificate, and reflective safety vest.

> **Saurav Goyal, Chief Operating Officer, Food Marketplace, Swiggy said,** "Our delivery partners are at the heart of everything we do, and we remain committed to building solutions that support their professional growth and enable them to have a better future. Through this exclusive partnership with Hero MotoCorp, we are making vehicle ownership more accessible with curated pricing, flexible financing, and a seamless purchase journey designed specifically for our delivery partners. We are hoping that the initiative will enable more delivery partners to join us and earn more.”

> **Ashutosh Varma, Chief Business Officer, Hero MotoCorp shared,** "At Hero MotoCorp, we believe mobility is a powerful enabler of opportunity and economic progress. Our partnership with Swiggy reflects our commitment to making reliable, affordable mobility accessible to India's delivery partners, empowering them to enhance their earning potential while benefiting from Hero's trusted products and extensive service network. Equally important, by integrating road safety training into this initiative, we are reinforcing our commitment to safer roads and rider well-being. Together, we are creating holistic mobility solutions that support livelihoods and promote responsible riding.”

**The partnership will be enabled through an API integration connecting the Swiggy app with Hero MotoCorp’s systems.** Delivery partners can register their preferred vehicle on the platform and access the applicable vehicle and financing benefits.

![Furlenco’s Revenue Grows 2.6X in Two Years, Profit Touches Rs 59.5 Cr in FY26](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-03T120414.320.jpg)

Furniture rental platform Furlenco continued its growth momentum in FY26, reporting a significant rise in both revenue and profitability. **The Bengaluru-based company posted revenue of over Rs 370 crore and a profit of nearly Rs 60 crore, marking a strong performance two years after Sheela Foam acquired a 35 percent stake in the business.**

**Furlenco’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 370.43 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 228.74 crore in FY25.** Since FY24, when the company reported revenue of Rs 140 crore, its operating income has expanded by more than 2.6 times.

**Furlenco offers furniture and home décor rentals along with relocation services.** Rental income remained the primary contributor to its business, accounting for 92 percent of operating revenue. Revenue from furniture rental services increased 64 percent year-on-year to Rs 341.07 crore in FY26. **Meanwhile, revenue generated through product sales grew 38 percent to Rs 29.36 crore during the same period.**

**In addition to its core business income, the company earned Rs 4.99 crore from other sources, taking its total income to Rs 375.42 crore in FY26, up from Rs 240.05 crore in the previous fiscal year.**

**On the expenditure side, Furlenco witnessed a sharp increase in several key cost heads.** Depreciation expenses rose 57.5 percent, while finance costs climbed 75.6 percent during the fiscal year. Employee benefit expenses increased 17.1 percent to Rs 36.18 crore, and material costs nearly tripled to Rs 27.01 crore.

**The company did not disclose a detailed breakdown of other operating expenses, which were classified under miscellaneous expenses.** These costs increased 34.4 percent to Rs 181.04 crore in FY26 from Rs 134.7 crore a year earlier. As a result, Furlenco’s total expenditure grew 45.1 percent year-on-year to Rs 343.85 crore.

**Despite the increase in costs, revenue growth significantly outpaced expenditure expansion, leading to a substantial improvement in profitability.** The company’s profit surged to Rs 59.52 crore in FY26 from Rs 3.11 crore in FY25, representing a nearly 19-fold increase.

**Furlenco also reported strong gains in operational efficiency. Its EBITDA nearly doubled to Rs 129.5 crore during the fiscal year, while EBITDA margin improved to 35.01 percent.** Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) rose to 13.17 percent from 5.37 percent in the previous year.

**The company further strengthened its financial position, spending Rs 0.93 to generate every rupee of operating revenue compared to Rs 1.03 in FY25.** Cash and bank balances more than doubled to Rs 75 crore, while total current assets increased 67.9 percent to Rs 178 crore by the end of FY26.

Plum, a direct-to-consumer beauty and personal care brand, reported a strong financial performance in FY26, with revenue surpassing the Rs 500 crore mark and profits nearly doubling amid growing consolidation in India’s D2C beauty sector. 

**Revenue from operations increased 28 percent year-on-year to Rs 515 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 402 crore in the previous fiscal.**

Established in 2013, Plum offers a range of skincare, bodycare, fragrances, haircare and gifting products. **The brand sells through its own digital platform as well as leading e-commerce marketplaces including Amazon, Nykaa and Flipkart.**

**Product sales remained the company’s sole source of operating revenue during the year**. In addition, Plum generated Rs 14.3 crore through interest income and gains from mutual fund investments, taking its total income to Rs 529.3 crore in FY26.

**The company continued to invest significantly in brand building and customer acquisition.** Advertising and promotional expenses rose more than 32 percent to Rs 184.4 crore during the fiscal year, making it the largest component of its expenditure. Material consumption costs also increased 28 percent to Rs 184.4 crore, while employee benefit expenses grew 12 percent to Rs 47.6 crore. 

**Plum also incurred expenses related to warehousing, commissions, transportation, legal services, and other operational activities.** As a result, the company’s total expenditure stood at Rs 481 crore in FY26.

**Driven by robust revenue growth, Plum’s profitability improved considerably during the year.** Net profit rose to Rs 49 crore in FY26 from Rs 25 crore in FY25, reflecting nearly twofold growth. The company spent Rs 0.93 for every rupee earned from operating revenue during the fiscal year.

**The improved financial performance was also visible across key profitability indicators.** Plum reported an EBITDA margin of 8.12 percent in FY26, while its Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) increased to 13.2 percent. **The company closed the fiscal year with current assets worth Rs 305.6 crore, including Rs 92 crore in cash and bank balances.**

**Over the years, Plum has secured more than $50 million in funding through multiple investment rounds.** Its largest funding round came in March 2022, when it raised $35 million in a Series C round led by A91 Partners, with participation from existing investors Unilever Ventures and Faering Capital.

The company operates in India’s highly competitive D2C beauty and personal care market, where it competes with brands such as Juicy Chemistry, WOW Skin Science, Mamaearth and SUGAR Cosmetics.

![E-commerce Startup DealShare Considers Acquisition Amid Leadership Exits and Business Contraction](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-08/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-08-31T115504.233.jpg)

DealShare, the e-commerce platform known for selling groceries and household essentials, is reportedly evaluating acquisition opportunities with online pharmacy platform **TrueMeds and seafood and meat retailer Captain Fresh as it seeks a path forward amid prolonged business challenges.**

Discussions between DealShare and both potential acquirers are currently underway. However, no definitive agreement has been reached. Sources indicated that if neither transaction progresses, **the company could be forced to discontinue its operations.**

**DealShare is effectively at a point where it has two options: find a buyer or shut down.** The discussions with TrueMeds are more advanced than those with Captain Fresh, but nothing has been finalised yet.

**Over the past few years, the company’s business has contracted significantly following declining revenues and multiple restructuring efforts.**

DealShare does not have much of a business left to acquire. If the deal goes through, it would largely be a money-transfer transaction rather than TrueMeds buying a meaningful e-commerce business.

**TrueMeds and DealShare share a common investor in WestBridge Capital, which could potentially support ongoing discussions between the companies.** Captain Fresh, meanwhile, has been pursuing growth through acquisitions and expansion across the fresh food and retail sectors. **The company also shares investor connections with DealShare through Matrix Partners India, now rebranded as Z47.**

**DealShare has faced mounting operational pressures in recent years.** During FY24, the company reportedly laid off more than 100 employees and exited its B2B business segment as part of a restructuring initiative. Despite these measures, revenue continued to decline.

Financial filings show that **gross revenue from operations fell 13.4 percent to Rs 432 crore in FY25, down from Rs 499 crore in FY24 and Rs 1,963 crore in FY23.** While the company succeeded in reducing losses to Rs 87.65 crore in FY25 from Rs 167 crore a year earlier, it has yet to file its FY26 financial results.

**Founded as a social commerce and value-focused e-commerce platform, DealShare achieved unicorn status in January 2022 and has raised approximately $393 million from investors including Tiger Global, ADIA, Alpha Wave and Kora Investment.** Its last significant funding round was a $45 million investment from ADIA, secured at a valuation of $1.7 billion shortly after the company entered the unicorn club.

D2C home and sleep solutions brand Wakefit posted growth in both revenue and profitability during the first quarter of FY27, supported by continued expansion of its offline retail network and improved operational efficiency.

**For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported operating revenue of Rs 404.9 crore, registering a 17 percent year-on-year increase.** Profit after tax (PAT) rose 19 percent to Rs 23.4 crore during the same period. On a sequential basis, however, profit was lower compared to the previous quarter, primarily due to increased tax expenses following the deferred tax credit benefit recorded in the fourth quarter of FY26.

**Wakefit also recorded an improvement in its operating metrics.** Operating EBITDA grew 50 percent year-on-year to Rs 36.8 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded to 9.1 percent from 7.1 percent in the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting stronger cost management and business efficiency.

**The company's offline retail business continued to play a significant role in driving growth.** During the quarter, Wakefit added 27 company-owned and company-operated (COCO) stores, helping its retail business grow 21 percent year-on-year.

**With the latest additions, the company's store network increased to 165 outlets, compared to 138 stores in the preceding quarter.** The expansion is part of Wakefit's broader strategy to strengthen its omnichannel presence and complement its digital-first operations with a larger physical retail footprint.

According to Executive Director Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, **the company remains on course to open nearly 80 COCO stores during FY27 as part of its ongoing expansion plans.**

**To support this growth strategy, Wakefit has allocated between Rs 100 crore and Rs 120 crore in capital expenditure for the current financial year.** Approximately 80 percent of the investment will be directed toward retail expansion, particularly larger-format jumbo stores, while the remaining funds will be used for manufacturing automation and operational enhancements.

![Deepinder Goyal's Temple eyes Rs 4,785 crore valuation, prices first wearable at around Rs 80,000](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-07/goyal.jpg)

Founder of Eternal, Deepinder Goyal's healthtech startup Temple is eyeing to raise fresh capital at a valuation of approximately USD 500 million (Rs 4,785 crore), while pricing its first wearable device at around Rs 80,000.

Reports suggest that the price is still suggestive and will include lifetime access to Temple's software platform. Goyal is also offering its customers with a lifetime supply of the adhesive tapes used to attach the pebble-shaped deice to the side of the forehead, near the temple.

As opposed to smartwatches and rings that capture signals from the wrist or finger, Temple's aim is to get a richer source of physiological data from the temple region of the head.

The startup is positioning the wearable around healthy ageing and longevity, arguing that measurements taken from the temple could reveal physiological insights beyond conventional metrics such as heart rate.

This device is expected to be targeted initially at high-performance athletes, professionals and health-conscious consumers willing to pay a premium for continuous metabolic and recovery data.

Earlier this year, Temple raised approximately USD 54 million at a valuation of around USD 190 million. If the proposed funding round is completed at USD 500 million, then it would be more than double the startup's valuation within months.

**With the new role, Kareena Kapoor Khan's association with the brand extends beyond marketing.** She will contribute to the company's design selection process and support efforts to enhance brand visibility across domestic and global markets.

Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has moved a step closer to its planned initial public offering (IPO) after receiving observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

According to its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), the IPO will include a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 150 crore along with an offer for sale of up to 28.4 million equity shares by existing shareholders. Geetansh Bamania, the company’s founder and CEO, is listed as the promoter.

**The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for repayment of debt, payment of lease rentals or license fees for warehouses and experience stores, and for general corporate purposes.**

Founded by **Bamania, Rentomojo operates a direct-to-consumer online rental and subscription platform for furniture and home appliances.** The company provides flexible subscription options through both its digital platform and physical presence.

As of September 30, 2025, Rentomojo had 227,511 live subscribers across 22 cities. Its operations include 67 experience stores and 21 warehouses, supporting a portfolio of 728,773 products.

The company claims to hold an estimated 42–47 percent share in India’s organised home furniture and appliances rental segment.

In terms of financial performance, Rentomojo reported revenue from operations of Rs 176.61 crore for the six months ended September 30, 2025, with a profit after tax of Rs 61.38 crore. For the full financial year FY25, the company recorded revenue of Rs 265.96 crore and a profit after tax of Rs 43.11 crore.

Jaipur-based coffee chain Nothing Before Coffee has received investment commitments during its appearance on the startup show Bharat Ke Super Founders. ***The brand secured two offers from investors as it continues to expand its presence across India.***

Investor interest in Peping is driven by the company’s focus on functional nutrition and early signs of repeat consumption among customers. ***The brand operates within India’s premium and health-focused beverage segment, which is estimated to be valued at around Rs 10,000 crore and continues to grow.*** Functional beverages are among the fastest-growing sub-categories and are projected to reach Rs 13,500 crore by 2033, supported by increasing demand from Gen Z and millennial consumers seeking alternatives to sugary drinks.

***Founded by Chirag Maheshwari and Prateek Maheshwari, Peping produces low-calorie prebiotic fizzy drinks and probiotic digestive shots designed for daily consumption.*** The company aims to offer functional beverages that combine taste, affordability, and shelf stability for Indian consumers.

The brand’s product range includes sodas intended for regular consumption and digestive shots aimed at targeted gut health support. ***This format allows the company to address different consumption occasions within the functional beverage category.***

Peping products are currently available through quick commerce and e-commerce platforms, including Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, and BigBasket, as well as First Club, Namdhari’s, and Ratnadeep. ***The company also sells through more than 200 retail outlets in Bengaluru and has distribution partnerships with gyms, cafés, and corporate offices.***

***To improve margins and operational control, the company has set up its production facility using off-the-shelf components and manages soda canning in-house.***

> Chirag Maheshwari, Co-Founder, Peping said, “***We are thrilled to welcome IAN Group on board alongside key co-investors Signal Ventures, Eleven Eleven, and other angels. Beyond sharing our excitement for Peping’s vision, they bring invaluable strategic expertise to accelerate our distribution expansion and strengthen brand presence.***”

***Within the company, Chirag Maheshwari manages production, online sales and branding. Prateek Maheshwari oversees distribution, offline sales and finance.*** The founders have known each other since childhood and bring experience across product development, partnerships, and scaling operations.

Globally, functional sodas have gained traction, with brands such as Olipop and Poppi seeing strong growth in markets like the United States. In India, the category is still developing, though consumer interest in digestive health remains high. ***Industry data indicates that nearly 70 percent of urban Indians report digestive concerns, while traditional probiotic foods such as curd and kanji remain widely consumed.***

With the expansion of quick commerce and faster delivery networks, distribution opportunities for new beverage brands in India have increased, enabling companies in emerging categories to reach consumers more quickly.

![Farmley Nears Rs 400 Cr Revenue in FY25 with Improved Financials](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-12/Untitled%20design%20-%202025-12-31T121636.748.jpg)

Farmley, the healthy snacking brand, recorded a significant improvement in its financial performance in the fiscal year ending March 2025—a momentum that helped the company secure its $40 million funding round at the beginning of FY26. **The brand saw strong topline expansion and tighter cost discipline, with operating revenue rising sharply and losses narrowing despite continued scale-up.** Revenue from operations jumped 71 percent to Rs 394 crore in FY25, up from Rs 230 crore in FY24.

**Founded in 2017 by Akash Sharma and Abhishek Agarwal, Farmley sells a wide range of healthy snack products, including makhana-based snacks, date bites, roasted nuts, trail mixes, and seeds.** The company’s entire FY25 revenue came from the sale of these snacking products. Its total income grew to Rs 396 crore, from Rs 231 crore in the previous fiscal.

**On the expense front, cost of materials remained the largest cost component, forming 67 percent of total expenditure.** This cost increased 57 percent to Rs 281 crore in FY25, up from Rs 178.5 crore in FY24. Meanwhile, advertising and promotional spending doubled to Rs 52 crore. Employee costs rose 69 percent to Rs 27 crore, and logistics spending increased 54 percent to Rs 20 crore during the year.

**Overall, Farmley’s total expenses rose 63 percent to Rs 419 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 257 crore in FY24.**

Even with this rise in spending, the company’s strong revenue growth helped reduce losses. **Net loss declined 15 percent to Rs 22.5 crore in FY25, down from Rs 26.5 crore in the previous year.** The firm’s ROCE improved to -51.56 percent, while EBITDA margin strengthened to -3.68 percent.

**At a unit economics level, Farmley spent Rs 1.06 to generate every rupee of operating revenue in FY25—an improvement from Rs 1.12 in FY24.** The company closed FY25 with current assets of Rs 163 crore and cash and bank balances of Rs 22 crore.

**Farmley has raised $55 million to date, including the recent $40 million Series C round led by L Catterton.** Co-founders Akash Sharma and Abhishek Agarwal collectively hold a 52 percent stake in the business.

**The healthy snacking sector—also covering dry fruits such as almonds and cashews—has seen strong momentum, fuelled by rising consumer awareness and higher disposable incomes.** Farmley appears to have secured meaningful distribution partnerships across quick-commerce and other retail channels, which have contributed to its revenue surge. However, such channels may pressure margins, making future financial outcomes worth watching closely.

![Loca Loka joins India’s rising tequila wave](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-11/loca.jpg)

***Loca Loka, co-founded by Sree Harsha Vadlamudi, Rana Daggubati and Anirudh Ravichander, has entered India’s premium spirits market as demand for agave-based products continues to climb.*** The brand launched internationally in late 2024 across the US and Southeast Asia and has since expanded distribution across several global markets. India will now see the introduction of its Blanco and Reposado variants.

Created in India and produced in Jalisco, the brand brings together Mexican distillation practices and Indian creative influence. ***Loca Loka has built visibility in duty-free and export markets and has also earned recognition at major international competitions.*** Its debut in India reflects a focused expansion into urban retail and on-trade environments.

***To mark its entry, the brand hosted an invite-only tasting where the founders spoke about the tequila’s profile and production approach.*** Guests sampled serves highlighting the Blanco’s agave-forward character and the Reposado’s barrel influence, presented for both neat consumption and cocktail applications. The launch also included curated experiences in Delhi and Mumbai designed around the brand’s visual identity, developed with mixologists and technologists.

Loca Loka Blanco and Reposado, which were awarded medals at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition 2025, New York International Spirits Competition, Miami World Spirits Competition and the WSWA Wine and Spirits Tasting Competition in Denver, will be available in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, along with airport duty-free outlets. ***The rollout aligns with India’s expanding tequila segment, which is projected to exceed USD 76 million in 2025.***

> Sree Harsha Vadlamudi said, ***“Loca Loka is a business built on craft and clarity that ranges from sustainable agave sourcing to barrel strategy and global placement. India is a market that’s shifting to premium, and our rollout is designed to meet that shift with measured distribution and trade partnerships that respect the category.”***

> Commenting on the launch, Rana Daggubati said, ***“Storytelling is the spine of this brand because it’s not just a bottle, it’s a cultural remix. Loca Loka lets us celebrate two worlds at once: Mexico’s terroir and India’s colour and rhythm. The launch will be a narrative in motion.”***

> Anirudh Ravichander added, ***“The first sip tells you what careful distillation and intelligent maturation can do. Our Blanco and Reposado are crafted to deliver clear agave expression with layered subtleties making them bottles that perform both on the rocks and in signature cocktails. And here’s a little secret: the yeasts actually ferment better with music. This time, they worked to a playlist of my own tracks. Let’s just say the tasting notes might hit a few unexpected high notes.”***

> Master distiller Willy Bañuelos Ramírez, who oversees production in Jalisco, noted, ***“Bringing Loca Loka to India feels like the most natural next chapter in our journey. India has an instinctive appreciation for craftsmanship, purity, and flavour, qualities at the heart of our 100 percent agave tequila. Watching Indian consumers explore tequila with such curiosity and confidence is exciting for us as distillers. With Loca Loka, we’re creating a new conversation between Mexico’s agave heritage and India’s evolving, adventurous palate. This launch is a cultural crossover we’re proud to pour.”***

The India launch arrives at a time when the category is expanding. ***The Indian tequila market reached USD 600.1 million in 2024 and is expected to grow to USD 1.68 billion by 2033 at a CAGR of 12.1 percent.*** Agave-based spirits in India grew by 36 percent by volume in 2024.

Loca Loka plans to support its India rollout with B2B partnerships across premium bars, hotels and duty-free retail. ***The brand will also conduct curated tastings and market activations through 2026, reinforcing its position in the premium spirits landscape.***

Honasa Consumer Limited, the parent company of brands like Mamaearth and The Derma Co has announced its entry into the prestige skincare segment with the launch of a new brand, Luminéve. The brand, which is created specifically for night-time use, is debuting exclusively on the e-commerce platform Nykaa. bi

Luminéve is built around the concept of the skin's natural nocturnal repair cycle and circadian rhythm. The brand introduces a "***night-first***" approach to skincare, with formulations designed to work in sync with the body's biology. ***The core idea is that the skin behaves differently at night, when it shifts from a defensive mode to a repair and regeneration mode.*** During this period, the skin's barrier strengthens, cell turnover accelerates, and it becomes more receptive to treatments.

At the heart of the brand's formulations is a proprietary blend called the Advanced NightRenew Complex. ***This complex contains a mix of actives and botanicals such as Collagen, Peptides, Niacinamide, and Polyglutamic Acid, which are encapsulated for a time-release delivery.*** This technology is designed to release the active ingredients in sync with the skin’s natural rhythm throughout the night.

> Ghazal Alagh, Co-Founder and Chief Innovation Officer at Honasa Consumer Limited said, “***Night skincare has long been treated as an extension of day routines, but the skin doesn’t follow our convenience; it follows its own biology. During the day, the skin is in defence mode, shielding itself from stressors. At night, it shifts into repair and regeneration mode, it absorbs better, loses more moisture and responds most effectively to targeted treatment. Luminéve is built to respect this science. It is purposeful, precise and designed for the time when skin naturally repairs the most, across different skin types.***”

Luminéve is launching with a curated collection of clinically tested night moisturizers tailored to six distinct skin types. ***The range also includes overnight serums that feature India’s first Liposomal Technology with ingredients like Vitamin C, Niacinamide, Retinol, and Salicylic Acid.*** This technology is intended to help the active ingredients absorb more effectively through the night while remaining gentle on the skin.

The products were developed by Honasa’s in-house R&D team in collaboration with Korean formulation experts and a global dermatologist, ensuring that the formulations are both high-performance and suitable for Indian skin. ***The decision to launch exclusively on Nykaa is a strategic one, as the platform is a key destination for consumers seeking premium and prestige beauty products.***

***With this launch, Honasa aims to strengthen its presence in the fast-growing prestige skincare category.*** The brand is catering to a segment of consumers who are increasingly looking for science-backed, intentional routines and are influenced by dermatological recommendations. The products will be available at a price range of Rs 1499 to Rs 1799, positioning Luminéve firmly in the premium-to-prestige space.

![Indo Count Revives Iconic Wamsutta Brand with D2C Launch in the U.S.](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-07/Untitled%20design%20%2870%29.jpg)

Indo Count Global, the U.S. subsidiary of Indo Count Industries Ltd. (ICIL), has announced the strategic relaunch of Wamsutta, one of America’s most recognized legacy home textile brands, as a direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform. The brand’s premium bedding and bath collections are now exclusively available on its D2C website in the United States.

This relaunch follows Indo Count’s acquisition of Wamsutta from Beyond, Inc. in April 2024 and is part of the company’s broader strategy to strengthen its presence in the U.S. premium home textiles market. The move signifies Indo Count’s shift towards owning customer relationships directly, with a focus on digital-first distribution and consumer engagement.

> “Wamsutta has always stood for superior quality and comfort that endures. Now, with refreshed branding, premium positioning, and a direct-to-consumer approach, we are connecting with a new generation of consumers while continuing to honour the brand's legacy and deepen our relationship with longtime loyal customers who have trusted Wamsutta for decades,” said Mohit Jain, Executive Vice Chairman of Indo Count Industries.

The newly launched  D2C website offers a curated collection of premium products that emphasize quality, simplicity, and timeless aesthetics. The D2C model allows Indo Count to connect directly with consumers, gather real-time insights, and adapt its offerings swiftly in response to market feedback. It also strengthens the company’s ability to build long-term brand equity through digital storytelling and customer engagement.

The Wamsutta relaunch also aligns with Indo Count’s continued focus on premiumization and sustainability. The company recently achieved a Dow Jones Sustainability Indices (DJSI) score of 66 in 2024, placing it among the top 10% in the global Textile, Apparel & Luxury Goods sector—well above the industry average of 30. Indo Count has also earned multiple awards for its sustainable manufacturing practices and maintains strong financial ratings, including ICRA AA- and CARE AA- for long-term facilities and A1+ for short-term credit.

By reintroducing Wamsutta as a digitally native brand, Indo Count seeks to reinvigorate a legacy name with modern relevance. The D2C model will play a pivotal role in creating personalized customer journeys, deepening engagement, and driving agile product development—all of which are key to scaling the brand’s growth in today’s competitive U.S. home textile market.

The relaunch represents more than just a brand refresh—it’s a strategic move to anchor Indo Count’s ambition of becoming a dominant player in the global premium and branded home textiles space.

![Retail India News: Proventus Agrocom Delivers Strong FY25 Results, Expands Reach and Innovation Pipeline](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-05/Untitled%20design%20-%202025-05-23T121229.671.jpg)

Proventus Agrocom Limited (NSE: PROV), announced its audited financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2025, marking a significant milestone in its journey toward becoming a Rs. 1000 crore brand by FY28. The company reported consolidated revenue of Rs. 584 crore, reflecting a 16 percent year-on-year growth. Its brand revenue saw a sharp 37 percent rise to Rs. 417 crore, driven by expanding market presence and growing consumer demand. Gross margins improved to 19.8 percent from 17.6 percent in FY24, while EBITDA rose by 8 percent to Rs. 12.9 crore. Despite doubling its investments in brand building, the company registered a 3 percent increase in profit after tax (PAT) at Rs. 7.4 crore, with earnings per share (EPS) standing at Rs. 21.40.

> “*FY25 was a defining year for ProV — one in which ambition translated into execution. We expanded, innovated, invested, and delivered. We remain steadfast in our mission to become a Rs. 1000 Cr brand by FY28, backed by quality, scale, and consumer trust,*” **shared Durga Prasad Jhawar, Managing Director, Proventus Agrocom Ltd.**

The company’s brand-first strategy led to a sixfold growth in brand sales over the last three years, with over two crore product pouches sold during FY25—a testament to strong consumer adoption. **These results came alongside a significant increase in brand-building investments, underscoring the company’s commitment to long-term market leadership.**

ProV also continued strengthening its operational and manufacturing capabilities. **It is currently on track to commission a fourfold capacity expansion at its Surat facility, increasing output from 1.5 lakh to 4 lakh pouches per day.** Operational efficiencies remained strong, with a 97 percent On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery rate. Additionally, the company focused on enhancing its leadership team, onboarding 22 key hires across sales, marketing, and operations to support its next phase of growth.

**The company saw notable gains across its distribution channels. Modern trade accounted for 46 percent of total brand sales, up from 34 percent in the previous year.** Quick commerce (Q-Commerce) operations were launched, and e-commerce grew by 32 percent year-on-year. General trade also saw significant expansion, with the company’s footprint now covering more than 15,000 outlets across India.

In terms of product innovation, FY25 witnessed the launch of several new SKUs, including premium dates, chocolate-coated nuts, and gifting packs. These offerings aligned with ProV’s focus on premiumisation and health-forward snacking formats. **The brand now boasts a robust portfolio of over 175 SKUs across six product lines, catering to a wide spectrum of consumers.**

Looking ahead, ProV’s strategic focus for FY26 includes deepening its general trade presence in Tier II and Tier III towns, scaling its Q-Commerce and direct-to-consumer (D2C) channels, and continuing to innovate with new product formats and seasonal ranges. **The company also plans to strengthen its leadership team further and digitise operations to drive greater efficiency**. On the marketing front, it aims to optimise media spends, enhance brand storytelling, and expand sampling initiatives to deepen consumer engagement.

> “*With a brand-first strategy, a high-performing team, and investments in infrastructure and innovation, we are building a future-ready business. FY25 was about delivery. FY26 is about scale — with purpose, profitability, and precision,*”  **stated Durga Prasad.**

As Proventus Agrocom accelerates its momentum, the results of FY25 underline its strong foundation and commitment to building a scalable, consumer-centric brand in India’s fast-growing health and wellness sector.

![Retail India News: Myntra Introduces MynShakti, Strengthening Women’s Role in E-Commerce](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2025-02/Untitled%20design%20-%202025-02-26T114353.721.jpg)

Bengaluru-based fashion e-commerce giant Myntra has introduced its exclusive Women Seller Program, ‘MynShakti,’ aimed at empowering women entrepreneurs across India. **The initiative is designed to provide aspiring businesswomen with essential tools, resources, and mentorship to help them navigate and succeed in the competitive e-commerce landscape.**

**In its initial phase, MynShakti intends to onboard around 100 women sellers, offering tailored support to facilitate their seamless integration onto the Myntra platform.** The program is committed to fostering business growth and financial independence, driving positive change, and enabling women-led enterprises to achieve their aspirations.

> “*MynShakti is a natural extension of Myntra’s ShECommerce initiative. Through MynShakti, we are creating a dedicated support system for women entrepreneurs, equipping them with the right resources to navigate e-commerce. This initiative is not just about business growth—it’s about enabling financial independence, fostering leadership, and driving meaningful change. We are excited to welcome a new wave of women-led brands to Myntra and look forward to seeing them flourish*,” **said Govindraj MK, CHRO, Myntra.**

Women-led brands participating in MynShakti will receive comprehensive support through a seamless onboarding process and dedicated account managers to help optimize business performance. They will also undergo hands-on training sessions that cover essential aspects such as catalog optimization, pricing strategies, and operational efficiency to enhance their competitiveness. **Additionally, interactive mentorship sessions and expert-led webinars will provide strategic guidance on marketing, order fulfillment, and maximizing Myntra’s platform potential.**

Women entrepreneurs interested in participating can apply via a survey link available in Myntra’s LinkedIn post about the program. **The initiative will commence with a webinar to introduce shortlisted candidates to Myntra’s seller ecosystem. Based on the pilot phase’s success, Myntra aims to expand the program to support a wider network of women entrepreneurs across the country.**

MynShakti builds upon the foundation of ShECommerce, Myntra’s flagship initiative launched in August 2024 to enhance women’s participation in e-commerce. **ShECommerce currently includes a thriving community of over 6,000 members and key programs such as ShE-roes Unplugged, which features webinars where industry leaders share insights and experiences.** Additionally, it offers an internship and mentorship program for college students, particularly in Tier II and III cities, bridging the gap in access to role models and career opportunities.

![Retail India News: Haier Appliances India Set to Surpass $1 Bn Revenue in 2024](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-12/Untitled%20design%20-%202024-12-30T183411.133.jpg)

Haier Appliances India is poised to achieve a significant milestone in 2024, surpassing $1 billion in revenue, driven by robust summer sales, festive demand, and the ongoing trend of premiumisation, according to the company’s President, N.S. Satish. T**he company is targeting revenue of Rs. 11,500 crore in 2025, after projecting ₹8,900 crore for 2024.**

“***2024 has been one of the best years we ever had, with a growth of 35 percent. We will be a one-billion-dollar company this year. Next year, our target is Rs. 11,500 crore***,” Satish shared.

**Haier operates on a January-December financial cycle and attributes this rapid growth to strong performances across all categories, especially LED TVs and washing machines.** The rising trend of premiumisation has boosted average selling prices, contributing to Haier’s fastest growth rate in the appliances sector.

**Despite this success, Satish highlighted India’s low market penetration compared to global benchmarks, presenting vast growth opportunities.** “*The Indian market offers a huge opportunity, and we are addressing it by aligning our products accordingly,*” he stated. Haier aims to differentiate itself through India-specific innovations and unique offerings in segments such as refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, and LED TVs.

The company is also diversifying into commercial air conditioning and kitchen appliances, segments experiencing rapid growth. “***We are still setting up our basic infrastructure for these products, including manufacturing and after-sales services, which need to be strong***,” Satish explained.

Haier has already invested Rs. 2,500 crore in India and plans to establish a third manufacturing facility in southern India by 2026 or 2027. “*We have started scouting for land. Discussions and proposals are underway,” said Satish. The new facility will serve both domestic and export markets*.

**In addition, the Greater Noida plant is undergoing expansion under Phase II, adding backward integration capabilities such as injection molding and sheet manufacturing.**

India is Haier Group’s third-largest market globally, after China and the U.S., where it competes with brands like Samsung, Panasonic, Whirlpool, Bosch, and local players such as Godrej and Voltas.

![Retail India News: ONDC Network Surpasses 12 Mn Monthly Orders in July](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-08/Untitled%20design%20-%202024-08-05T170522.565.jpg)

The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) has achieved a significant milestone as it has recorded 12 million monthly orders across various categories, with daily orders reaching 430,000 in July 2024. **The network currently has over 638,000 sellers and service providers, operating in more than 609 cities and delivering to 1,200 cities nationwide.**

**Category-wise, the mobility sector, such as ride-hailing applications, accounted for 4.4 million transactions.** The remaining 7.6 million orders were from non-mobility sectors. Within this non-mobility segment, the food and beverages category saw 1.7 million transactions, while groceries accounted for 1.4 million transactions. **The fashion segment contributed 0.6 million transactions, with the remaining 4 million orders spread across on-network logistics, beauty and personal care, home and kitchen, and retail vouchers.**

Speaking of the food & beverages sector, the network has captured 18 percent market share in Bengaluru and 3 percent nationally, indicating strong adoption in key markets. Additionally, July saw the launch of the auto components and accessories category on the network, featuring sellers such as Ess Aay Automotive.

Established on December 31, 2021, the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is a Section 8 company initiated by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. ONDC aims to revolutionize digital commerce by creating a facilitative model that enhances the penetration of retail e-commerce in India. **ONDC is not an application, platform, intermediary, or software but a set of specifications designed to foster open, unbundled, and interoperable open networks.**

![{Funding Alert} Moxie Beauty Secures Rs. 17.3 Cr Funding Led by Fireside Ventures](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-07/Untitled%20design%20%2875%29.jpg)

Gurugram-based D2C haircare brand Moxie Beauty has successfully raised Rs. 17.3 crore (USD 2.1 million) in a funding round led by Fireside Ventures. **The round also saw contributions from a distinguished group of angel investors, including Samir Singh (former Unilever CMO Personal Care and Chair Unilever Asia), Arjun Purkayastha (Regional CEO at a leading MNC), Suhasini Sampath (Founder of Yoga Bar), and Navin Parwal and Sangeet Agrawal (Founders of Mokobara).**

Founded in November 2023 by Nikita Khanna and Anmol Ahlawat, **Moxie Beauty specializes in salon-quality hair care products designed specifically for Indian hair textures.** The brand's offerings include shampoos, conditioners, leave-in products, and styling solutions aimed at addressing dryness and frizz.

> “*India is not on the R&D roadmap for most global brands - they don’t formulate their products for Indian hair types, weather, or habits, which are very different from Western ones. For so long we have been taught to see our hair as ‘unruly’ and ‘unmanageable’ – but there is no such thing as bad hair, only unsuitable routines that were not made for us. Moxie’s mission is to empower people with the right products, tools, and knowledge to care for and feel confident in their natural hair texture*,” **said Nikita Khanna.**

**Khanna, an MBA from XLRI, was previously a consultant at McKinsey & Company, while Ahlawat, an MBA from FMS, held the position of General Manager at Paytm.**

> “*We are very excited to partner with Moxie Beauty. It ties in well with our fund thesis of investing in purposeful brands that are innovating for the new Indian consumer. Moxie’s approach to building products suited for Indians who have wavy, frizzy and curly hair is a refreshing innovation in the large and growing hair care and beauty space*,” **shared Dipanjan Basu, Co-Founder and Partner at Fireside Ventures.**

The newly acquired funds will be directed toward product innovation and research, talent acquisition, and expanding distribution channels. With its focus on innovative products and a mission to empower consumers, Moxie Beauty aims to capture a significant share of India’s USD 5 billion haircare market.

Nasher Miles, a prominent digital-first luggage brand renowned for its vibrant and stylish designs, has successfully completed a $4 million bridge funding round, elevating the company's valuation to $30 million. **This new influx of capital positions Nasher Miles for accelerated growth and expansion following its recent success on Shark Tank India.**

**The bridge round attracted more than 40 investors, including notable figures such as Singularity Early Opportunities Fund, Narendra Rathi (Investment Director at SoftBank Vision Fund), Sulabh Arya (Executive Director at Goldman Sachs Growth Equity), and Mohit Goyal (Ex-Managing Director at CVC Capital Partners).** This diverse group of investors underscores the strong confidence in Nasher Miles' business model and its growth potential. The company’s pre-money valuation of $25.32 million reflects a 5.5 percent premium over its Shark Tank valuation, demonstrating the brand's commitment to sustainable growth. Much of this funding was facilitated by Avinash Rajpal.

> **Lokesh Daga, Co-founder & Director, Nasher Miles said**, "*This funding round is a testament to the strength of our brand and our vision for the future. We've strategically opted for a smaller raise at a reasonable valuation, setting the stage for our Series A round later this year or early next year. This approach allows us to maintain our growth momentum while preparing for larger-scale expansion. Our USP is variety. We see ourselves as a fashion player in the luggage industry, offering an unparalleled range of colors and designs. This funding will enable us to bring our innovative products to more customers across India through multiple channels*."

The newly acquired funds will primarily be used to support Nasher Miles' ambitious omnichannel expansion plans. **The company aims to increase its offline presence to 1,000 multi-brand outlets across India by the end of the calendar year and open 3-5 exclusive brand outlets this financial year.** Additionally, Nasher Miles plans to enhance its quick commerce presence in select cities and boost its production capacity in India, with a goal of achieving 70-75 percent domestic manufacturing by December 2024. These strategic initiatives are designed to strengthen Nasher Miles' market position and foster sustainable growth across various channels.

Nasher Miles has already made significant progress in expanding its offline presence, appointing over 20 distributors nationwide and establishing a presence in 150 stores within just two and a half months. The company projects that its offline channel will generate $12 million in revenue in the next financial year.

Looking ahead, Nasher Miles aims to achieve over $60 million in revenue by FY 2028, aspiring to establish itself as a leading omnichannel brand present across all possible sales channels in India.

![{Funding Alert} Newme Secures $18 Mn in Series A Funding](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-07/H%26M%20Move%20and%20Special%20Olympics%20Bharat%20Uniting%20for%20Inclusive%20Sports%20Empowerment%20%284%29.jpg)

Gen Z-focused fashion-tech startup Newme has successfully raised $18 million in Series A funding, spearheaded by venture capital firm Accel, with significant participation from existing investors such as Fireside Ventures and AUM Ventures. This fresh infusion of capital is set to fuel the company's ambitious growth plans and further cement its position in the burgeoning fashion-tech industry in India.

> “*With this investment, we are well-positioned to accelerate our growth and empower a whole new generation of fashion-conscious consumers in India. We are dedicated to addressing the dual-fold challenge of design relevance and evolving shopping preferences with precision and insight,*” **said Sumit Jasoria, co-founder, Newme**.

**The newly acquired funds will be strategically utilized to enhance the brand’s omnichannel presence, establish a robust network of offline stores, and optimize its tech-driven supply chain.** This move aims to create a seamless shopping experience for consumers, blending the convenience of online shopping with the tactile satisfaction of in-store purchases.

> “*Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands are uniquely positioned to capitalise on India’s retail sector, which is set to cross $2.2 trillion by 2030, leveraging omnichannel strategies. We are excited to partner with Newme on its journey to a leader in the fashion-tech industry in India*,” **said Anand Daniel, partner at Accel.**

**Earlier this year, Newme secured Rs 45 crore in seed funding from Fireside Ventures, AUM Ventures, 2 AM Ventures, and Allin Capital.** These early investments laid the groundwork for Newme's rapid growth and helped the company establish a strong foothold in the competitive fashion market.

**Founded in 2022 by Sumit Jasoria, Vinod Naik, Shivam Tripathi, and Himanshu Chaudhary, Newme has rapidly emerged as a key player in the fashion-tech sector, targeting more than 500 million Gen Z customers in India and Southeast Asia.** The brand's innovative approach combines cutting-edge technology with contemporary fashion, appealing to the digital-savvy youth demographic.

Currently, the online-first brand operates six stores across five cities. However, Newme has ambitious expansion plans. In the next 12-18 months, the company aims to open 40-50 stores across 20 cities, including regions like Guwahati, Shillong, and Imphal. This expansion will not only increase the brand's physical presence but also enhance its ability to connect with a wider audience.

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Havells India Reports 42 Pc Increase in Q1 Net Profit, Reaching Rs 407.51 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-07/Untitled%20design%20%2826%29.jpg)

Havells India Ltd announced a significant 42 percent increase in consolidated net profit, reaching Rs 407.51 crore for the first quarter ending June 30, 2024. This impressive growth is attributed to robust sales driven by a scorching summer. In comparison, **the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 287.07 crore in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year, as stated in their regulatory filing.**

**The company's consolidated revenue from operations in the first quarter was Rs 5,806.21 crore, a notable increase from Rs 4,833.8 crore during the same period last year.** Total expenses for the quarter also rose to Rs 5,334.54 crore, up from Rs 4,516.59 crore a year ago.

The electrical consumer durables segment reported revenue of Rs 1,055.42 crore, compared to Rs 877.52 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. **The Lloyd brand of consumer products generated revenue of Rs 1,928.72 crore, a significant rise from Rs 1,310.92 crore in the same period last year.**

**The cables business segment recorded revenue of Rs 1,521.24 crore, up from Rs 1,485.18 crore in the corresponding quarter of the last fiscal year.**

In an investor presentation, Havells India attributed the robust sales growth to the extremely hot summer, which boosted demand across various product categories. The company noted that the industrial and infrastructure segments continued to perform well, though there was some impact from the elections. Additionally, **the company highlighted its commitment to brand building, with 3 percent of its revenue allocated to advertising and sales promotion during the first quarter, reinforcing its market presence and consumer engagement.**

Looking ahead, Havells India expressed optimism about the demand outlook, citing positive consumer trends and an uptick in market activity. The company remains focused on leveraging these trends to sustain its growth momentum and further enhance its market share.

![Urban Company Gives 200x Return to Their Investors](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2024-07/Untitled%20design%20%2825%29.jpg)

Urban Company has announced the successful conclusion of the investment journey of Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, founders of Snapdeal and Titan Capital respectively. **They initially invested Rs 57 lakh in 2015, and their recent exit transaction, facilitated by Dharana Capital, yielded aggregate proceeds of Rs 111 crore.** This transaction underscores the confidence and growth potential they perceived in Urban Company.

**In addition to Bahl and Bansal, several employees participated in the secondary deal, aligning their interests with the company's continued success.** Vamsi Duvvuri, founder of Dharana Capital, will join the board as a non-executive director, bringing valuable insights and support.

> “*Urban Company has built an enduring and growing business with a strong foundation. We have been fortunate to be part of this journey from its earliest days and immense credit is due to Abhiraj (Singh Bhal), Varun (Khaitan) and Raghav (Chandra) and their team for building it with great determination, resilience and foresight*,” **Titan Capital stated in a statement.**

**Bahl and Bansal have indicated that 100 percent of their gains from Urban Company will be reinvested to support the next generation of Indian startups, aligning with their commitment to fostering entrepreneurial innovation.**

**Urban Company continues to strengthen its market position and expand its service offerings, supported by strategic investments and operational milestones.** The company's revenue for the April-June period of this year stands at Rs 282-283 crore, marking a profitable quarter with a clear path towards sustained profitability by FY25.

**Titan Capital continues to scout for early-stage startups, recently investing in Boba Bhai, Karban Envirotech, and DevDham.** Both Bahl and Bansal also promote Unicommerce, an ecommerce enterprise software developer set to go public.

In the past year, Bahl and Bansal sold shares worth around Rs 78 crore through the IPO of Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth. They saw returns of over 100 times on their investment and committed to reinvesting these gains into other startups.

Urban Company continues to focus on delivering exceptional services and driving innovation in the home services industry.

Heads Up For Tails (HUFT) has unveiled Hearty, a groundbreaking dry food product aimed at transforming pet nutrition in India. **Developed after extensive collaboration with top canine nutritionists and veterinarians, Hearty underscores HUFT's commitment to providing pets with top-tier quality and wholesome nutrition.**

Hearty stands out by using 100 percent real, locally sourced farm-fresh ingredients, completely free from byproducts, fillers, and artificial additives. Each ingredient is carefully chosen, and the recipe is gently baked in small batches at low temperatures to preserve essential nutrients like proteins, fats, fibers, vitamins, and minerals, surpassing the nutritional profile of conventional dry foods.

**The formula includes proteins and omega fatty acids from meat, eggs, and fish, fiber from premium vegetables, fruits, and grains, and essential vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants from a variety of sources.** Additionally, Hearty is enriched with Indian super herbs like Ashwagandha, Tulsi, Moringa, Giloy, and Turmeric, known for their holistic health benefits, enhancing overall pet wellness and setting a new standard in pet nutrition.

**Hearty's production process ensures consistency and excellence, with each batch containing 60 percent real meat content and up to 50 percent fresh ingredients, far exceeding typical dry foods.** This dedication ensures pets receive optimal nutrition with every serving.

> **Samarth Narang, CEO, HUFT shared**, “*We are excited to launch Hearty, a product that epitomizes our commitment to pet health and well-being. By utilizing the finest ingredients and advanced preparation methods, we believe Hearty will significantly enhance the lives of pets across India*."

> **Rashi Narang, Founder, HUFT added**, "*Hearty is not just another dry food brand; it represents our pledge to provide pets with the nutrition they deserve. Our meticulous research, careful ingredient selection, and thoughtful packaging all reflect our dedication. Hearty is a testament to our promise to deliver excellence to our pets*."

Hearty is now available online at headsupfortails.com and at over 90 HUFT stores nationwide, offering pet parents a convenient and nutritious solution for their pets' well-being.
